# Client history audit 2026-10-01

Evidence for the "Client history" sections on client pages. Rank 7 (chat-derived). Not reviewed.

chunks.heading: Method
chunks.text:
- Source: every Assembly message channel and message, read-only (2025-07-10 → 2026-10-01). Channels matched to Hub clients by Assembly ids, with name / email fallbacks listed in [[audits/spine-2026-10-01]].
- Each message was passed through the support bot redactor before any model saw it, and capped in length. Raw transcripts stay outside the repo.
- Stage A: paid DeepSeek V4 Flash extracted dated notes per client. Stage B: paid DeepSeek V4 Pro wrote the per-client summary. OpenRouter with provider data collection denied; $15 hard cap.
- Total model cost: 0.203404 usd.
- On pages: model text re-redacted; links, emails, dollar amounts and percentages replaced with placeholders (numbers from chats are not verified).
- Excluded: Blackbird internal client, RevFactor Test Client, Josh Burdick (Blackbird), Kristine Gilden (merged into Juan Taiana), and the unmapped "Beard & Braid" channel.

chunks.heading: Gaps
chunks.text:
- **GHL CRM is unreadable by agents.** Contacts, tags, sources, pipelines, opportunities (won/lost/value), conversations, tasks, payments, templates and custom fields all return 401. Pipeline numbers are **unknown**. Fix: a GHL export, or a token with those scopes.
  - Update 2026-10-05: **mostly closed.** The `prod-ghl-mcp` connector reads contacts, custom fields, pipelines and opportunities. Aggregates: [[evidence/ghl-crm-2026-10-05]]. Still open: won/lost and dollar values are not filled in GHL, and conversations, tasks and payments were not tried.
- **Lead source is mostly unknown:** 117 of 153 Hub leads and 140 of 143 HoneyBook projects. `lost_reason` is never filled.
  - Update 2026-10-05: in GHL, 11 of 68 live contacts have no source and 47 skipped "how did you hear". No GHL opportunity has a lost reason.
- **Credentials outside the Hub:** 6 incidents (email, Granola notes ×2, Slack, iCloud note, sales rep). See [[policies/data-and-secrets]].
- **Proration and billing rules** for a mid-month setup and for two-card payment are unwritten (Slack 2026-09-15, 2026-09-28).
- **A "fixed 12% fee from Oct 29"** needs a client broadcast, but which party charges it is **unknown** (Granola 90a5fe86 2026-09-29).
- **Report pipeline:** 78 of 138 PriceLabs report runs failed (Hub).
  - Update 2026-10-05: every run since 2026-10-01 failed (`session_expired`); last good run 2026-09-30. See [[review/R-020-report-builder-not-running]].
- **Knowledge base:** 2 of 19 articles are approved for the agent; the onboarding and offboarding guides are still drafts (Hub).
- **Contract terms per client:** the Drive contract PDFs are scans with no text, so per-client terms are not machine-readable.
- **Agentmail notifications** stop at 2026-09-28. Possibly a gap in forwarding.
- **Unmatched people in meetings:** a "Lisa" offboarding in June (listing for 14 guests), a "Lucas" (Dallas area), "Cori/Cory" (matched to [[clients/past/cory-huddleston]] by context, not by id), and "Top Tier Estates" in Slack are not tied to a Hub id. Prospects (Brandy Gray, Simon Bindloss, Ruby Tiwari and others) have no Hub client.
- **Slack coverage:** only the newest 100 messages per channel; older history and bot channels were not read.
- **Granola** covers only Fede's calls. Ethan's and Emily's calls are not recorded anywhere agents can read.

# Needs Listing Review check: Teresa Le (2026-10-08)

Evidence. Read on 2026-10-08 via the `prod-ghl-mcp` connector (contact, opportunity, conversation), Gmail (Fede's mailbox), Granola, and the Hub (read-only SQL). Nothing was changed in GHL, the Hub or Gmail, and no one was messaged. No email, phone or street address is stored here.

Teresa Le is a **lead**, not a client, so she has no `clients/` page. GHL contact `wtPXpcepHBIqcgm84WTX`, opportunity `3sWbwUlH0fnY1JuhbJZ9`.

chunks.heading: Questions asked by Fede
chunks.text:
1. Did we build a workflow for the "needs analysis" outcome? **Yes.**
2. Did she get the email? **Yes. GHL logged it as sent, but it can't show whether she opened it.**
3. Did she complete it? **No, not through the workflow.** She sent the address another way (see below).

chunks.heading: Timeline
chunks.text:
| when (UTC) | event | source |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-05 22:09 | Booked a Discovery Call from revfactor.io. Source "RevFactor Discovery Call"; heard via Referral (Jane Ng). Property "Live and taking bookings". Airbnb link saved in the contact `website` field. | GHL contact |
| 2026-10-05 22:10 | Opportunity created in **RevFactor Sales → New Lead**. Confirmation email and SMS sent; SMS reminders went out on 10-06 and 10-07. | GHL conversation |
| 2026-10-07 20:00 | Discovery call with Emily. Appointment marked completed. | GHL activity; Granola `e28f9efe` |
| 2026-10-07 20:20 | Opportunity stage changed from New Lead to **Completed Call**. | GHL activity |
| 2026-10-07 20:26 | Contact field **RF Post-Call Outcome** (`contact.rf_postcall_outcome`) set to `4 — Needs listing review`. | GHL contact `dateUpdated`, field value |
| 2026-10-07 20:26:39 | **Workflow email sent**, subject "Send us your listings for review". It asks for up to 3 listing links plus questions and goals by reply. Message `source: workflow`. | GHL conversation |
| 2026-10-07 20:29 | Emily emails Fede and Gaston. Teresa wants specific comps for her property, plus before/after data from a *comparable* RevFactor property (the deck examples weren't close enough). Emily sends the listing link. Fede asks for the exact address. | Gmail |
| 2026-10-08 00:13 | Email "Address of listing" on the GHL thread: Emily asks Teresa for the exact address so she can pull comps. GHL logged it as **inbound**, which looks like a sync oddity. | GHL conversation |
| 2026-10-08 15:41 | Emily sends Fede the exact address. At the same time, contact@revfactor.io (Emily) replies to Teresa: "Got it! Get back to you soon." | Gmail; GHL conversation |

chunks.heading: Findings
chunks.text:
- **The workflow exists and fired.** The option-4 email went out about 4 seconds after the outcome was set. The connector can't read workflows, so its exact name and steps are **not on file**. The send is proven by `source: workflow` on the message.
- **"Delivered" is not proven beyond "sent".** There is no bounce or error on the record, and the connector doesn't expose opens. The one tracked-link click on the contact came from a link sent at 20:20:05. No message to Teresa went out at that time, so it was most likely the internal post-call link sent to the closer. It is **not** evidence that Teresa engaged.
- **She did not complete the workflow ask.** No reply to "Send us your listings for review" is in GHL. `RF Listing Review Link`, `RF Property Address`, `RF Airbnb Listing URL` and `RF Listings Submitted` are all empty. No Hub listing-review intake exists for her (`listing_review_requests` has 1 row ever, a draft from 2026-09-17). She is not in Hub `leads` either.
- **She did give Emily the exact address** (10-08), but outside the workflow. Her reply isn't in the GHL thread, and the address wasn't written back to GHL.
- **Commitment at risk:** on the call, Emily said she'd send comps and before/after data by **2026-10-09** (Granola). Teresa's goal is to onboard before the Thanksgiving/Christmas peak.
- **No owner or task on the deal:** the opportunity has `assignedTo: null`, 0 notes and 0 tasks, and it still sits in Completed Call. The workflow doesn't create a task, assign anyone or set a reminder.

chunks.heading: What she asked for (Granola `e28f9efe`, 2026-10-07)
chunks.text:
- Property: a 2-bed / 2-bath cabin in Sevierville, TN (Smokies), with hot tub, sauna and pro photos. Owner-occupied about 6 months a year. 41 five-star reviews; top-5% host.
- Stack: OwnerRez PMS, PriceLabs (self-run), Vrbo inactive.
- Goal: hand off dynamic pricing across short, medium and long booking windows; stop making weekly manual edits; capture more revenue.
- Wants: (a) ADR, occupancy and RevPAR for comparable 1–2 bedroom Smokies properties; (b) RevFactor before/after on a comparable managed property.

chunks.heading: Gaps found in the process
chunks.text:
1. The option-4 email is generic. It asks for links we often already have (here, the Airbnb link came from booking) and doesn't ask for what the analysis needs: the exact address, PMS/PriceLabs access or an export, and the last 12 months of revenue.
2. Nothing tells the team that option 4 fired. No task, no owner, no due date, and the opportunity stays in Completed Call.
3. The Hub intake built on 2026-08-30 (secure upload link, 48h reminder planned) is not wired to option 4 and has never been used.
4. Data collected by email (the address) isn't written back to GHL fields.
5. GHL's outcome field has 5 options. [[funnel/sales-funnel]] lists 6 (including "Needs Call with Fede"). Option 6 is not in the live GHL field.

# Onboarding journey, as-is (2026-10-12)

Draft for Fede. This maps how onboarding actually runs from the sales call to day 90. It covers the onboarding calls added in September and lists the gaps and the steps that are missing.

**Sources:**
- 8 Granola onboarding calls (Sep 2 to Oct 12) and the sales calls before them.
- Hub SQL, read-only: `onboarding_*`, `adjustments` where type = setup, `listings`, and `pricelabs_reservations_bq`. The cohort is 35 clients created since 2026-06-01.
- GHL pipelines, custom fields and the onboarding calendar.
- Slack: #revfactor-onboarding (33 daily boards), #revfactor-main-chat, #revfactor-cos, #revfactor-sales.
- The HostPricing WhatsApp chat (1,303 messages since Jun 1).

Credentials that appeared in these sources are excluded.

Related: [[playbooks/onboarding-v2]] (the to-be flow, decided 2026-10-12), [[playbooks/onboarding]] (the old intended steps) and [[funnel/onboarding-pipeline]] (the earlier evidence page). The goals work is [[playbooks/comp-analysis]].

Pricing preferences come up in the last 5–10 minutes. Goals or break-even were captured on only 1 of 7 calls. Floors were left TBD for Brandy and Jacob. About 45% of India setups needed an access follow-up. Blue's 6 setups have been in `needs_info` since Oct 1. |

Patricia's listing was pushing prices before the setup was stamped. Blocked calendars stopped prices from pushing (Florence, Lake Como). |

chunks.heading: Gaps, ranked
chunks.text:
1. **The owner's economics are never captured.** No form asks for the break-even amount (the Assembly form asks only "do you know it?"). The current GHL form has no revenue target, floor or minimum stay. Floors have no payout-vs-guest basis, and 5 of 9 differ from the PriceLabs minimum. This is the root cause of the floor and minimum-stay complaints in weeks 1–2.
2. **The onboarding call has no RM block.** It is roughly 80% access and channel hygiene. Pricing inputs get the last few minutes, and only when Fede runs the call (Emily's call collected none).
3. **No handoff artifact between steps.** Sales call → onboarding call → setup brief is passed along in private Granola notes, chat and memory. India asked for an owner-context sheet on Jul 6; it was never built.
4. **The setup has no spec and no QA gate.** Briefs are empty or done by analogy. The control step is a click (median 46 h, batched), yet a third of setups need fixing within 30 days.
5. **Launch is undefined.** There is no go-live stamp, no launch pack record and no first-booking watch, so day 30, 60 and 90 cannot be computed.
6. **The first 90 days are unowned and reactive.** No check-ins, no first report, no review against target.
7. **Access gating is wrong.** Setup starts before access is complete, so "done" is partial and go-live slips by days.
8. **Too many systems, with stale state.**
   - Three intake systems.
   - The checklist is ticked in batches and lags reality by about 5 days.
   - The onboarding calendar is never marked showed or no-show.
   - GHL deals are not marked won, which matters because the commission webhook needs `status=won`.
   - Run notifications: 18 failed vs 12 sent.
9. **Scope and expectations drift on calls.** Free direct-booking sites, Hospitable setup and Vrbo builds get offered on some calls, while clients on other calls hear "we don't set up channels". Calls booked for 30 minutes run up to 2.5 hours, and client questions are left without an owner (Moin, Brandy, Jacob, Kasey).

| Where | Step | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Before the call | **Prep pack:** a sales handshake (goal, pain, promises, blocks, scope), plus a listing audit and market support from comps | One page read by whoever runs the call |
| On the call | **RM block (15 min, scripted):** break-even (amount + period), owner goal, floor (payout basis), min-stay policy, owner blocks, events, priorities, decision-maker, report cadence; then show goal vs market and agree on a target | Per-listing goals record in the Hub |
| On the call | **Expectations and scope statement:** setup date, launch pack, first report, response time, what is and is not included | The same text every time |
| After the call | **Access gate:** setup starts only when the co-host, PMS and PriceLabs are verified | Checklist state in the Hub, not chat |
| Setup | **Setup brief generated from the goals record** (no free text) | A standard India ticket |
| Setup | **QA checklist before sync is turned on** (floor, minimum stay, blocks, markups, calendar open, PMS dynamic pricing off) | Control step with checks |
| Launch | **Go-live stamp** (first push) and a **launch pack** template | `live_at` + a sent record |
| Days 1–14 | **Pickup watch:** alert if there is no booking N days after go-live | Hub alert |
| Day 30 | First review + first monthly report vs target pace | A report record |
| Day 60–90 | Goals check: re-anchor the target, or have the gap conversation | Update to the goals record |

chunks.heading: What the pilot taught us about the loop
chunks.text:
1. Log every pricing promise as an adjustment, with nights. Without nights, we cannot pick the dates to watch.
2. `resolved_at` is the team's click, not the PriceLabs change. PriceLabs logs would give the real time.
3. Split OTA from direct. Direct bookings can hide or fake a pricing effect.
4. Check what else changed in the window (minimum stays, blocks, go-live) before giving a verdict.
5. One client gives too few changes. Run it portfolio-wide and pool by type. The Hub has 74 applied pricing adjustments with dates.

# BRAIN

RevFactor company map. Agents read this first. They do not load the whole vault.

chunks.heading: What we do
chunks.text:
Revenue management for short-term rental owners. We set PriceLabs pricing, minimum stays and channel settings on clients' Airbnb / Vrbo listings, and send reports and recommendations. We do not manage properties and we do not give real estate advice.

Team: Fede (owner, final say), Gaston (co-founder: accounts, billing, Stripe), Andrés (revenue manager: pricing recs), Martín (client messages in Assembly). See [[people/team]].

chunks.heading: What matters now
chunks.text:
1. Client and listing spine: every client and listing has its ids first ([[Clients]], [[Listings]]).
2. Clear the id mismatches in [[audits/spine-2026-10-01]] before any bot uses those clients.
3. Client history summaries are evidence until Fede reviews them ([[audits/client-history-2026-10-01]]).

chunks.heading: How work is structured
chunks.text:
Objects, actions and the exception → decision → outcome loop: [[ontology/README]]. New processes and tools follow it.

Every new framework or playbook starts with the four-step **Deepen first** block in `_templates/playbook.md` (Fede, 2026-10-14): what a top revenue manager would add, the rawest material, the named methods, and an outside check that proves the result.

chunks.heading: Source order (when sources disagree)
chunks.text:
1. What Fede has cleared ([[Decisions]]). That wins.
2. The Hub (Supabase `revfactorHub`): clients, listings, reservations (`pricelabs_reservations_bq`; revenue = `total_cost` per v1, disputed: [[review/R-016-official-revenue-number]]), billing mirror.
3. PriceLabs: live pricing truth per listing.
4. Stripe: billing truth.
5. Signed contract and onboarding form.
6. This vault (accepted facts only).
7. Assembly chats, Slack, email, call notes. Evidence only.

Dates only break ties between two sources of the same rank.

chunks.heading: Rules
chunks.text:
- Audit before write: fact, value, source, date and rank go in an `audits/` file; Fede reviews; then the client or listing page, citing the audit. Never silently pick a winner.
- Every change to a client or listing fact adds a dated row to its `## History`.
- Missing answer: write "not on file". Never turn a guess into knowledge. Never invent numbers.
- No passwords, logins, one-time codes, API keys or card numbers anywhere (files, commits, PR text). Write "in Hub credentials".
- Client chats: summarize with date and source. No long verbatim quotes.
- Revenue advice only. Purchase questions get revenue estimates; the client decides.
- Never message clients or staff from this vault's work.
- Skip lists: [[clients/_past-clients]] and [[listings/_exited]]. Never import those as live.
- Generated pages ([[Clients]], [[Listings]], [[Markets]], [[Decisions]], [[Stack]], [[Audits]], [[Processes]], [[Evidence]], [[Funnel]], [[Review]], [[Skills]]) come from `tools/brain/build_hubs.py`. Don't hand-edit them.

chunks.heading: Layers
chunks.text:
- **Knowledge**: `clients/`, `listings/`, `policies/`, `playbooks/`, `skills/`, `stack/`, `people/`, `fleet/`, `markets/`, `decisions/`, [[learnings]].
- **Evidence**: `audits/`. Dated and never company knowledge on its own.
- **Work**: Notion, RevFactor HQ → Board and Projects. Not in this vault.

chunks.heading: Folder map
chunks.text:
- `clients/<slug>.md` — one per live client (active or onboarding); ids first. `clients/past/<slug>.md` — offboarded clients.
- `listings/<slug>.md` — one per live listing; ids first. Exited listings: [[listings/_exited]].
- `stack/` — tools and what each is the source of truth for ([[Stack]]).
- `playbooks/` — how we do things. `policies/` — company rules.
- `skills/` — pricing skills and frameworks we use and apply, one per file (template `_templates/skill.md`); index [[Skills]] (generated). RM shows the same list from `exports/pricing-skills.json` (`python3 tools/brain/export_skills.py`).
- `decisions/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` — settled, newest wins.
- `fleet/` — bots and what they may and may never do.
- `metrics/` — field registry and portfolio metrics ([[metrics/field-registry]], [[metrics/portfolio-metrics]]).
- `review/R-NNN-<slug>.md` — one open question per file where two sources disagree; index [[Review]] (generated).
- `_templates/` — page templates.

docs.title: Setup spec defaults and direct-cheapest rule (2026-10-13)

chunks.text:
# Setup spec defaults and direct-cheapest rule (2026-10-13)

**Decision** (Fede, in the RevFactor Operating System project thread, 2026-10-13):
1. **Floor:** break-even payout after channel fees, excluding cleaning, with the owner's "never below" price on top.
2. **Max price:** 3× base by default, plus event overrides.
3. **Gap-night premium:** +15% by default.
4. **QA waivers:** only Fede or Gaston can waive a failed setup QA check.
5. **Approval:** Fede approves every setup spec.
6. **Channels:** Booking.com and the direct site are in scope for the first setup. Direct is always the cheapest guest total, because owners always want direct below Airbnb.
7. **Booking.com markup:** the property's contracted commission + 5 points.
8. **Direct-site discounts:** copy Airbnb's length-of-stay discounts (trip length, weekly, monthly).

**Why:** the first setup had no template and no QA gate, and a third of setups were corrected within 30 days ([[audits/onboarding-journey-2026-10-12]]). These defaults let code draft a complete spec.

Related: [[playbooks/setup-spec]], [[playbooks/goals-and-targets]] (answers question 5).

chunks.heading: Stages and dispositions
chunks.text:
- After each discovery call the closer picks an outcome: Start Onboarding, Follow Up / Nurture, No-Show, Needs Analysis (audit), Not a Fit, and **Needs Call with Fede** (option 6). (Granola 5eb07771 2026-09-03; 66f5afe2 2026-09-16)
  - Live GHL (2026-10-08): this is contact field `RF Post-Call Outcome` (`contact.rf_postcall_outcome`) with **5** options: `1 — Start onboarding`, `2 — Follow up / nurture`, `3 — Not a fit`, `4 — Needs listing review`, `5 — No-show`. Option 6 "Needs Call with Fede" is **not** in the live field.
  - Option 4 fires a workflow that sends one email ("Send us your listings for review"). It creates no task, no owner and no reminder. Playbook: [[playbooks/needs-listing-review]]. First case: [[audits/needs-listing-review-teresa-le-2026-10-08]].
- Good fit → onboarding form → agreement → recurring Stripe payment → onboarding call. (Granola 66f5afe2 2026-09-16) From 2026-09-10 GHL owns the form, agreement, invoice and calendar ([[funnel/onboarding-pipeline]]).
- Sales call slot moved from 20 to 30 minutes, and a three-way text chain was set up with each lead (Granola 5eb07771 2026-09-03).
- Closers call immediately after "Book my call" to cut no-shows (Granola ad7bdc99 2026-07-28).
- The Hub lead grades A ideal / B needs evaluation / C not a fit date back to HoneyBook project types (Drive export; Hub `leads.service_type`).

chunks.heading: Recommendation (pending Fede)
chunks.text:
Open question from the 2026-10-04 handoff: which revenue and occupancy numbers are official?

1. **Revenue: use the bookings feed.** Take `rental_revenue` from `pricelabs_reservations_bq`. Spread it evenly over the stay's nights. Count status `booked` only. This is the owner report v5 rule.
2. **Occupancy: use the same feed.** Booked nights ÷ nights in the period. Show PriceLabs adjusted occupancy only as a cross-check.
3. **Report Builder: use for market numbers only.** Market ADR, market occupancy, RevPAR index and market pace. Always print its run date.
4. **Stop calling `total_cost` revenue.** It adds cleaning and guest charges. The Hub code never sums it.

Why:
- The feed matches Report Builder within 2% on 277 of 299 listing-months (September 2026).
- Every mismatch has a known cause. Six Marissa Biddle homes are double-counted in Report Builder (about +$105K in September). Twelve Airbnb-direct homes run 5–23% higher there.
- The feed refreshes daily and works. Report Builder has not finished a run since 2026-09-30.
- The feed is auditable to the booking. Report Builder is a PriceLabs total we cannot open.
- Feed occupancy matches Report Builder within 2 points for 214 of 234 homes.
- The Hub reservations page, the Excel export and owner report v5 already use `rental_revenue`.

Before this becomes official, three data fixes are needed:
- Unlink or exclude the Marissa Biddle twin listings ([[review/R-018-marissa-biddle-twin-listings]]).
- Decide gross or net for Airbnb-direct homes ([[review/R-019-airbnb-direct-revenue-gap]]).
- Fix Report Builder ([[review/R-020-report-builder-not-running]]).

Decision items: [[review/R-016-official-revenue-number]], [[review/R-017-official-occupancy-number]].

# Portfolio metrics

How each portfolio number is computed, then a dated snapshot. Field meanings and sources: [[metrics/field-registry]]. The revenue and occupancy rules below follow the registry recommendation. They are **pending Fede** ([[review/R-016-official-revenue-number]], [[review/R-017-official-occupancy-number]]).

chunks.heading: Rules used on this page
chunks.text:
- **Scope:** RevFactor clients only. Blackbird (billing entity `blackbird`) and `test` rows are out.
- **Active listing:** Hub `listings.status = 'active'` under a client with status `active` or `onboarding`.
- **Revenue:** `rental_revenue` ÷ `number_of_days`, given to each night from `check_in` to `check_out − 1`. Status `booked` only. One row per `reservation_key`.
- **Booked nights:** count of those nights.
- **ADR:** revenue ÷ booked nights.
- **Occupancy:** booked nights ÷ (active listings × days in the month). Owner blocks are not removed.
- **RevPAR:** revenue ÷ (active listings × days in the month).
- **STLY:** the same nights shifted back 364 days, counting stays booked by the as-of date minus 364.
- **Like-for-like YoY:** only listings that had at least one booked night in that month last year.
- **Pickup:** stays booked in the last 7 or 30 days, for any night, by `booked_date`.
- **As-of date:** 2026-10-04, the last feed fetch.

Core SQL (read-only; returns monthly revenue and nights):

```sql
with rf as (
  select l.listing_id lid from listings l join clients c on c.id = l.client_id
  where coalesce(c.billing_entity,'') <> 'blackbird' and l.status = 'active'
    and c.status in ('active','onboarding') and nullif(trim(l.listing_id),'') is not null
  group by 1),
res as (
  select distinct on (r.reservation_key) r.* from pricelabs_reservations_cache r
  join rf on rf.lid = r.listing_id where r.booking_status = 'booked'),
n as (
  select r.listing_id, r.booked_date, d::date night,
         r.rental_revenue / greatest(r.number_of_days, 1) rev
  from res r cross join lateral generate_series(r.check_in, r.check_out - 1, interval '1 day') d)
select date_trunc('month', night)::date mon, round(sum(rev)) revenue, count(*) nights
from n where night >= date '2026-09-01' and night < date '2027-01-01'
group by 1 order by 1;
```

# RevFactor ontology

This is the shared vocabulary for how RevFactor works: the things we track (**objects**), the only ways they change (**actions**), and the loop that makes every change measurable (**exception → recommendation → decision → execution → outcome**). People, the Grok bot, Claude and Codex all use these names.

This folder is the source of truth. Code repos keep only the technical mapping (tables, functions, routes), and that mapping links back here:
- Hub: `docs/ontology/listing-review.md`
- RM: `docs/ontology.md`, once Codex phase 0 lands

chunks.heading: Rules (Fede, 2026-10-12)
chunks.text:
1. **The Listing is the anchor.** Every object links to a Listing (canonical Airbnb ID, aliases kept) and/or a Client, plus an action. If something can't be linked, it doesn't go in.
2. **One way to change state.** Only named, permission-checked actions change anything. The UI, bots and Claude use the same verbs. Every action appends an audit row. PriceLabs stays read-only.
3. **Every exception follows the chain.**
   - **Exception:** a signal that something is off.
   - **Recommendation:** what to do, with the evidence frozen at that moment.
   - **Decision:** who approved it. Append-only.
   - **Execution:** what was actually changed, and where.
   - **Outcome:** measured later against a fixed metric.
4. **Exception is an interface.** Every source has the same shape: `listing · client · source · type · severity · opened · status · evidence · summary`. All of them land in one queue.
5. **Code computes the numbers.** That covers scores, targets, pace and RevPAR index. An LLM only writes the wording, using AI Gateway free models first.
6. **Thin slices.** Take one source and one action all the way to a measured outcome before adding the next.

chunks.heading: What the map says
chunks.text:
1. **The front half is mostly live in GHL** (stages 1–6). What's left there is small and known: the double-pick guard, the cancellation stop, payment nudges, Emily → Fede wording, and switching on the goals form (stage 7).
2. **The seam is the onboarding call.** Everything after it (stages 8–16) is designed in playbooks but not running. Goals, targets and the setup still pass through Fede's head and Granola.
3. **There is no journey record.** No single field says which stage a client is at, so day 14 / 30 / 90 can't be computed and nothing can alert on a stall. Proposed object: **ClientJourney** (one per client: stage, entered_at, owner, next action due), with listing-level stamps (goals approved, access verified, live_at, launch report sent) feeding it.
4. **The back half has no owner.** After the launch, nothing happens unless the client complains, and the day-90 contract change passes unnoticed.

4. **Setup spec and go-live stamp** (stage 13, PR #8).
5. **Launch report** (stage 14), built on the listing review.
6. **First 90 days:** pickup watch, day-14 check-in, day-30 report, day-90 touch point.
7. **Renewal and retention** (stages 19–20).

chunks.heading: Open questions (Fede)
chunks.text:
- Which slice first? Recommended: slice 1, because it is mostly done and every new client passes through it.
- Should there be a client-facing touch point at day 90, when the commitment ends?

# Comp analysis (comp analyzer v3)

**Status: draft, proposed 2026-10-08. Not yet approved by Fede.** The full spec and the Codex rebuild brief are in the RM repo at `docs/comp-analyzer-v3.md`.

- Owner: Fede approves comp sets and any number sent to a client or lead. The builder runs the steps (not on file yet).
- When to use: lead analysis ([[playbooks/needs-listing-review]] part A), purchase underwriting, new-build estimates, and client pricing setup.

chunks.heading: The rule: three checks, never one score
chunks.text:
1. **Fit:** same product for the same guests and trip (RM fit engine: rooms, amenities, location, design, signature).
2. **Competitive tier:** reputation and presentation (Guest Favorite, rating, reviews, Superhost, photos, search position). Tiers: Premium, Strong, Standard, Weak, New.
3. **Performance:** what the comp books and asks (trailing ADR, occupancy and RevPAR; asking rates for the next 90 days), always labeled booked or asking.

Only comps at fit Tier 2 or better **and** in the subject's tier or above may set rate targets or ceilings. Example: GameBarn was an 87% fit with 13 reviews, no badges and phone photos, so it can't set the Horse Farm ceiling.

chunks.heading: Steps
Do not
chunks.text:
- Don't pool booked rates, guest quotes, AirDNA asking rates, historical ADR and own revenue into one series.
- Don't treat unknown as no. Use "not captured" and "not checked".
- Don't use our own managed homes as the whole comp set; it's circular.
- Don't send comp or client names to a lead. Anonymize.
- Don't let a fit % set a price.

chunks.text:

- Code review of RM origin/main 9739d67 (2026-10-08).
- PriceLabs help: "Understanding comp sets in PriceLabs".

# Daily pricing (draft)

Status: deepening done, 2026-10-14. The method comes next, from the reframed brief below. Part of the client journey after go-live ([[playbooks/setup-spec]]). Ontology: [[ontology/README]].

chunks.heading: Deepen first
chunks.text: **The task as first stated:** what we watch on every live listing each day, which signals count as exceptions, and how each one becomes an adjustment Fede approves and we measure at 7 and 30 days.

chunks.heading: 1. What a top revenue manager would do that we weren't asking for
chunks.text:
- **Triage the portfolio by money, not by listing.** At 1,000+ listings nobody reviews every calendar. Rank every exception by **revenue at risk**: the gap between on-the-books and the target curve for the next 30, 60 and 90 days, in dollars. The team works the top of that list and nothing else.
- **Diagnose before touching the rate.** A listing that is behind may have a price problem, a restriction problem (min stay, gaps, a closed calendar) or a visibility problem (ranking, photos, conversion). Price is the last lever, not the first ([[playbooks/listing-optimization]], layer 1).
- **Treat "ahead" as a problem too.** Filling far-out peak dates early at a low ADR is lost money. Being ahead of pace with a low ADR means raise, not celebrate.
- **Watch the stay pattern, not only the price.** Orphan nights, a min stay that strands weekdays, and lengths of stay the market is booking that the listing blocks.
- **Change less, and measure properly.** Set a budget for changes per listing per week, freeze the evidence on each one, and compare against similar listings we didn't touch. Otherwise every outcome is an anecdote ([[processes/decision-outcome-loop]]).
- **Score the rules themselves.** Track how often each exception type led to a change that worked. Rules that don't predict anything get retired.

chunks.heading: 2. The rawest material to start from
chunks.text:
Not PriceLabs' dashboards, MPI, or Report Builder's monthly totals. Start from:
- **Every reservation with its booked date**, from `pricelabs_reservations_bq` (Hub, daily). From it we can rebuild on-the-books for each stay date at every lead time, which gives us real booking curves and pickup.
- **Daily snapshots of what we offered:** price, min stay and availability for each stay date, captured every day (PriceLabs `listing_prices`). Today's price alone can't tell us what was on offer when a date did or didn't book. RM already captures daily calendar snapshots for 48 listings (`rm_event_forward_snapshots`, from 2026-10-09).
- **PriceLabs Pricing Logs** for history: past pushes by push date and stay date.
- **Market forward occupancy and pace by stay date** (PriceLabs neighborhood data), plus comp calendars from RM.
- **The listing funnel** from RankBreeze: impressions, CTR, views, booking rate.
- **Our own changes:** the Hub `adjustments` log, with what changed and when.

chunks.heading: 3. Methods and tools
chunks.text:
- **Booking curves by lead time** for each stay month: on-the-books vs the approved target curve ([[playbooks/goals-and-targets]]) and vs market pace for the same stay dates.
- **Pickup analysis:** bookings in the last 7 days vs what the curve expects for this lead time.
- **Forward RevPAR index** by month: our on-the-books RevPAR ÷ market forward RevPAR.
- **Calendar scan:** orphan nights, stranded weekdays, closed or blocked dates, and dates priced at the floor or the max.
- **Rate vs pickup from snapshots:** did dates that were cut pick up, and did dates that were raised keep pace? This gives a rough read on how sensitive a listing is to price.
- **Exception score** = revenue at risk × how sure we are (data completeness, days to arrival).
- **Tools:** Hub reservations feed and SQL, the PriceLabs API (`listing_prices`, `bookings_report`), RM snapshots and event intelligence, RankBreeze, and the decision → outcome SQL.

chunks.heading: 4. What would show it's right, other than us
chunks.text:
- **RevPAR index vs the market for the dates that were stayed**, measured after the stay, not when we made the decision. Acted-on listings should improve their index more than comparable listings we didn't touch over the same dates (a difference-in-differences test).
- **A back-test on last season:** run the exception rules on last year's bookings and snapshots, and check whether they flagged the listings that later fell behind. Kate Henry's Gainesville drop is the first case.
- **Owner revenue vs the approved annual target**, at month end.
- Caveat: which revenue and occupancy numbers are official is still pending ([[review/R-016-official-revenue-number]], [[review/R-017-official-occupancy-number]]). Report Builder market data has been stale since 2026-09-30 ([[review/R-020-report-builder-not-running]]).

chunks.heading: Reframed brief
chunks.text: Write the daily pricing playbook as a **morning portfolio triage**. Each day, code rebuilds on-the-books for every live listing and stay date from the raw reservation feed and the daily offered-rate snapshots. It compares that with the approved target curve and with market pace, and ranks exceptions by revenue at risk, both behind and ahead of pace. For the top exceptions, an agent diagnoses whether the cause is price, restrictions or visibility, then drafts one adjustment with the evidence frozen. Fede approves, ops applies, and there is a weekly limit on changes per listing. The outcome is measured as the RevPAR index vs the market for the dates actually stayed, against untouched comparable listings. The rule set is back-tested on last season before it goes live, and each exception type keeps a hit rate.

chunks.text: To be written next.

# Goals and targets (draft)

Status: draft, 2026-10-13. Fede decides the open questions at the bottom. Part of [[playbooks/onboarding-v2]]. Ontology: [[ontology/listing-review-and-onboarding]] (object **OwnerGoal**).

chunks.heading: Why
chunks.text:
Owners judge us against a number, and today we rarely write it down. In the Oct 12 research across 100 clients:
- Only 18 had a break-even amount on file.
- 34 had a numeric goal.
- 9 had all three anchors (break-even, goal, market).
- 17 had none of them.

Goals usually ran 1.2–2× what comps support, and 2–3× break-even. The onboarding form only asks *whether* the owner knows their break-even. Most floor and minimum-stay complaints in weeks 1–2 trace back to this.

chunks.heading: The three anchors (per listing)
chunks.text:
| Anchor | What | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Break-even** | What the listing must earn to cover costs: amount + period, plus what it includes (mortgage, HOA, cleaning, utilities, management) | Owner (GHL form + call) |
| **Owner goal** | What the owner hopes for, and where that number came from (history, AirDNA, investor model, designer) | Owner |
| **Market support** | What comparable listings actually earn at this listing's quality tier | Comps (PriceLabs neighborhood data, comp method v3) |

chunks.heading: From anchors to targets
chunks.text:
- **Floor** = max(break-even, the owner's "never below" price), stated as **payout after fees**, not guest price. Turned into a PriceLabs minimum with the discount-ladder math (minimum = floor payout ÷ lowest ladder payout share).
- **Base target** = market support at the listing's tier:
  - Standard: P50 → P75
  - Strong: P75 → P90
  - Premium: P90 → top

  Raised toward the owner goal only as far as comps support. Year 1 uses the conservative comp level.
- **Stretch** = internal only. What we aim for if pace allows.
- **Monthly targets (12 months)** = target occupancy × target ADR per month (nightly revenue, excluding cleaning and taxes), after owner blocks.
  - Use the listing's own history only if nothing material changed.
  - Use last-year **market** pacing, not last-year owner pacing.
- **Target pace** = the market booking curve, i.e. the share of each month's target expected to be on the books at each lead time.
  - "Behind" means more than X points below the expected pace.
  - This one definition replaces the three that conflict today.

chunks.heading: Listing stage and history: what we can trust (Fede, 2026-10-13)
chunks.text: History is extremely useful, but only when it is comparable. A listing changes over time, and results earned under the owner's own (often weaker) management are not a target. Two rules come before any target is set.

chunks.heading: 1. Classify the listing stage (code decides from data, Fede can override)
chunks.text:
| Stage | Definition | How targets are set |
|---|---|---|
| **New** | No short-term rental history, or under about 90 days live | Market support only, at the conservative comp level, with a new-listing ramp (the first 60–90 days run below steady state). |
| **Changed** | Has history, but a material change happened inside the window we would use | Split history at the change date. Use post-change data if there are enough months; otherwise use market support, with pre-change data as reference only. |
| **Established** | 12+ months, no material change, comparable operation | Use history, but as an **index vs the market**, not raw dollars (see rule 2). |

chunks.heading: 2. Benchmark relative to the market, never raw past revenue
chunks.text:
- Convert each historical month into a **RevPAR index**: the listing's RevPAR ÷ market RevPAR for the same month and comp tier.
- History under owner management or another manager shows where the listing *started*, not its ceiling. A low index under self-management is the gap we close, not the target.
- Target revenue = target index (from the comp tier) × forward market RevPAR, using last year's market final and current market pacing. This keeps targets honest when the market moves and when management changes.
- Exclude or flag months that weren't normal operation: long-term rental periods, owner use, closures, renovations, permit caps (e.g. a 120-night limit), seasonal-only operation.

chunks.heading: Material changes (log them, every time)
chunks.text:
These happen constantly and change what "comparable" means.
- **Physical:**
  - renovation
  - furniture or design refresh (Kasey mentioned furniture changes on her call)
  - amenity added or removed (e.g. a hot tub added on one listing)
  - bedrooms or capacity
- **Listing:**
  - new photos
  - new title or description
  - listing re-created under a new ID, which loses its reviews and history
  - a big swing in reviews or rating
- **Operation:**
  - long-term to short-term rental (Kasey's Tamarack 30 was long-term rented until this year)
  - seasonal-only operation
  - permit or night caps (Kasey's Timber Ridge 3D: 120 days, ski season only)
  - holds for possible long-term rentals
- **Management:**
  - self-managed or another manager → RevFactor
  - PMS or channel-manager change
  - pricing tool change

An amenity or capacity change can move the listing into a different comp set (e.g. a hot tub tier or a different guest count; see [[skills/comps-guest-count]]). Market support is then recomputed with the new comps.

Where changes come from:
- the GHL form: "Has anything changed in the last 24 months? What and when?"
- the onboarding call (Granola notes)
- the listing review: a re-audit that finds new amenities or photos proposes a change automatically
- accepted `listing_content` adjustments
- PriceLabs and PMS changes

chunks.heading: The two red flags (raised on the onboarding call, with comps on screen)
chunks.text:
1. **Goal > market support.** Show the gap on day one and agree on the year-1 target. Never promise the goal.
2. **Break-even > market support.** This is an economics problem, not a pricing problem. Say so plainly and document it.

chunks.heading: Ontology
chunks.text:
- **Objects:**
  - **OwnerGoal** (per listing), linked to Listing and Client.
  - **ListingStage** (new / changed / established, with the reason).
  - **ListingChange**: type, date, source, expected effect, and whether it splits history. Linked to Listing, and to the Adjustment or ListingReview that revealed it.
- **OwnerGoal fields:** Fields:
  - break-even amount / period / includes
  - goal and its source
  - floor and floor basis
  - market P50/P75/P90 at setup and the comp tier
  - base target, monthly targets, target pace curve
  - approved by / when
  - stage at the time of approval
  - history window used, and changes excluded
- **Actions:**

  | Action | Who | Approval / logging |
  |---|---|---|
  | SubmitIntake | client, via the GHL form | — |
  | RecordCallNotes | agent, from Granola | Fede approves |
  | ComputeMarketSupport | code, from comps | — |
  | ProposeTargets | code | — |
  | ApproveTargets | Fede, then the owner approves the base target | — |
  | ReviseTargets | Fede | at season start or on a material change; append-only with reason |
  | RecordListingChange | owner (form), agent (from call notes or an audit diff), staff | team review |
  | ClassifyListingStage | code; Fede can override | logged |

- **Exceptions:**
  - `goal_above_market`
  - `breakeven_above_market`
  - `pace_behind` (vs the target curve, by lead time)
  - `floor_basis_unknown`
  - `targets_missing` (a live listing with no approved targets)
  - `change_unlogged` (a re-audit or PMS diff shows a change with no ListingChange)
  - `history_not_comparable` (targets built on history that spans a material change)
- **Outcome:** actual vs target at month end and on the target curve at days 14 and 30. RevPAR index vs comps and same time last year.
- **Numbers come from code** (market support, targets, pace). AI writes only the owner-facing explanation.

chunks.heading: Where it's captured
chunks.text:
- **GHL onboarding form (source):**
  - break-even amount, period and what it includes
  - goal and its source
  - minimum price and whether it's payout or guest price
  - min-stay and 1-night policy
  - owner blocks as date ranges

  See the form changes in [[playbooks/onboarding-v2]].
- **Onboarding call:** confirm the anchors, then show goal vs market and agree on the year-1 target.
- **Backfill:** a short Assembly form to existing clients without a break-even, starting with the clients whose goals conflict most with their market.

chunks.heading: Open questions (Fede)
chunks.text:
1. **Unit:** revenue for owners and RevPAR internally? (recommended)
2. **Visibility:** do owners see the base target, or only the agreed year-1 number?
3. **Tier:** who assigns Standard / Strong / Premium, and from which signals (comp tier from the audit, reviews, photos, amenities)?
4. **"Behind" threshold:** one number, or by lead time (e.g. 10 points under 30 days, 15 points beyond)?
5. ~~**Floor definition**~~ Decided 2026-10-13: break-even payout after channel fees, excluding cleaning, with the owner's "never below" price on top ([[decisions/2026-10-13-setup-spec-defaults]]).
6. **History window:** how many post-change months make "changed" history usable (e.g. 3 months for a refresh, a full season for a capacity or amenity change)?
7. **Ramp curve:** the new-listing ramp (e.g. 60% of steady state in month 1, 80% in month 2, 100% from month 3), or measure it from our own launches?
8. **Storage:** Hub per listing-month (recommended, so it's in the ontology), PriceLabs "Manage Goals", or both?

# Listing optimization (draft framework)

Status: draft, 2026-10-12. It feeds the **launch report** in [[playbooks/onboarding-v2]] (day 3–5), the day-30 review, and later re-audits.

Waiting on: the Grok bot's `listing-score-report` skill (Revié score: completion / structure / OTA style / SEO). Fede is getting it from Grok. Its four parts will become the client-facing 0–100 score in layer 2.

Related: [[playbooks/comp-analysis]] and [[skills/comps-guest-count]] (the guest-count framework comes later as its own client education piece).

chunks.heading: Principle
chunks.text: The work follows the guest funnel from Fede's RM framework: **ranking → click-through → conversion**. Find where the listing leaks first, then fix that stage. Never push a generic checklist.

chunks.heading: Inputs
chunks.text:
| Source | Gives | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Airbnb public page (Apify / browser) | Title, photos, description, amenities, reviews, badges | Public |
| Airbnb host editor (co-host on pms@) | Captions, photo tour rooms, description sections, policies, review responses, safety | Co-host accepted |
| RankBreeze | Funnel vs similar listings (impressions, CTR, views, wishlists, booking rate), rank by guest count × date range with page-1 prices, section grades, competitor photos and rates, change journal | RankBreeze account (refreshes are limited per day) |
| PriceLabs neighborhood data + comps | Market support P50/P75/P90, comp tier | Our account |
| Goals record (GHL → Hub) | Owner rules: pets, Instant Book, min stay, 1-night policy, blocks, permit / occupancy caps | Onboarding form + call |

chunks.heading: Layer 1: funnel diagnosis (where it leaks)
chunks.text:
| Symptom vs similar listings | Stage | Levers to check first |
|---|---|---|
| Low rank or impressions | Ranking | Price vs page-1 average at each guest count, min stay vs searched length of stay, calendar open window, Instant Book, policies, core amenities, exact pin, new-listing ramp |
| Good impressions, low CTR | Click-through | Cover photo, title, first 5 photos, displayed price incl. fees, badges, review count |
| Good CTR, low booking rate | Conversion | Description (first 500 characters), photo coverage of every claimed amenity, reviews and responses, house rules, cancellation policy, host profile, total price with cleaning fee |
| Ranks well only for some guest counts | Ranking (fit) | Real party-size demand vs listed capacity; see [[skills/comps-guest-count]] |

Worked example (Spencer, Horse Farm, RankBreeze, 2026-10-12): the listing has about 8× the impressions of similar listings, but a lower CTR (16.6% vs 19.0%) and a lower booking rate (14.8% vs 18.8%). It is on page 1 for 7–10 guests but on pages 2–3 for 4-guest searches. **So the leak is click-through and conversion, not ranking.**

chunks.heading: Layer 2: listing score (client-facing)
chunks.text:
- **Headline score:** Grok's 0–100 Revié score with its 4 parts (pending import).
- **Detail underneath:** the 16 dimensions of `~/.claude/skills/airbnb-audit` (title, cover, photo order, photo quality, captions, photo tour, profile, first 500 characters, the space, guest access, interaction, other notes, amenities, review responses, location, safety).
- **Cross-check:** RankBreeze section grades (policies, title, description, host profile, amenities, photos, badges, review scores). A big disagreement between the two gets a human look.

chunks.heading: Layer 3: guardrails (what tools miss)
chunks.text:
1. **Truth check.** Every claimed amenity needs a photo or copy behind it, and no suggested amenity is added unless it exists. Blue's listings had a hot tub, fireplace and theater claimed with no proof. RankBreeze suggested "waterfront", "lake access" and "elevator" for a horse farm.
2. **Airbnb rules.** No party wording on no-party listings (Blue's "BACH!"), no contact info, no misleading claims, and permit numbers wherever required.
3. **Owner rules.** Filter every suggestion through the goals record. Allowing pets, turning on Instant Book for everyone, or changing the min stay or capacity is the owner's decision. Present it as an option with the trade-off, not as a fix.
4. **Regulatory.** Respect occupancy and permit caps, and the tax setup (see the taxes topic, next).

chunks.heading: Standard checklist and ontology
chunks.text:
- Every audit fills the same checklist (about 50 checks, each `pass / thin / fail / na / not_checked`), defined once in Hub `lib/listing-optimization-checks.ts`. The score, part scores and grades are computed from it. The owner page always shows the same sections: suggestions where checks failed, "Looks good" where they passed.
- Ontology chain: a failed check is the **Exception**, the suggestion is the **Recommendation**, publish plus the owner's accept is the **Decision**, the `listing_content` adjustment is the **Execution**, and the check passing on the 30-day re-audit (later also the RankBreeze funnel) is the **Outcome**. Every action writes an event row. See [[playbooks/onboarding-v2]] for the onboarding side.

chunks.heading: Scope
chunks.text:
- Listing content only: title, description, photos, captions, amenities, house rules and guest settings, host profile. Pricing findings never go in the owner listing review (Fede, 2026-10-12); they belong to pricing work.
- Things only the owner can change in Airbnb (host profile: about, bio, profile questions) are owner tasks: say "you do this one" and link to https://www.airbnb.com/users/profile/about?context=host&editMode=true.

chunks.heading: Host view is required
chunks.text:
- The audit runs **as host**, not from the guest page. Use the RevFactor co-host session in Chrome (the profile logged into Airbnb as the RevFactor co-host; it opens `airbnb.com/hosting/listings/editor/<id>/details`). Read only: never save, toggle or log out.
- Check every editor section for empty fields: photo tour (rooms, task, unassigned photos), title, property type, sleeping arrangements, guests, description sub-sections, amenities, accessibility, location (neighborhood description, getting around, scenic views, location verification), booking settings, house rules, guest safety, cancellation, custom link, and the arrival guide (check-in method, directions, Wi-Fi present, house manual, checkout instructions, guidebooks).
- A guest-page-only audit is **partial**. Don't publish it to an owner (Jacob, 2026-10-12: the first draft missed the empty neighborhood and getting-around fields).

chunks.heading: Where changes are applied
chunks.text:
- First check the editor's settings: if a PMS / channel manager (Guesty, Hostaway, Hospitable…) syncs content to Airbnb, apply accepted changes **in the PMS**, or the next sync overwrites them. Airbnb shows which fields the PMS manages (Jacob's Guesty listing: everything except directions, property type, Wi-Fi, checkout instructions and a few amenities).
- The review records this as `channel_manager`, and every queued adjustment says where to apply. We apply these changes ourselves through RevFactor's PMS access (Fede, 2026-10-13).
- First published review: Jacob Raabe, 2026-10-13 (score 43, live in his Assembly "Listing Review" tab).

chunks.heading: Owner wording
chunks.text:
- Say where the change happens in Airbnb terms. Amenities: "Check “Dryer” in your Airbnb amenities" (Listing › Amenities), never "tag" or "add". Captions: "the label under each photo". Titles: "the name guests see in search".
- Show "Now" for every change, even when it is "Not checked".

chunks.heading: Layer 4: fix list
chunks.text:
- Rank each fix by funnel stage first (fix the leaking stage first), then by impact × effort.
- Each fix states the current state, the proposed change, why (which metric it should move), whether the owner must approve, and who applies it.
- At most **5 headline fixes** in the client report; the rest go in an appendix.

chunks.heading: Layer 5: approve → apply → measure
chunks.text:
1. The client approves or declines each fix (the planned approval tab; until it exists, an Assembly message).
2. We apply the change through the co-host seat. **No auto "Push to Airbnb"** without approval.
3. Log each change as a Hub adjustment (type listing) with its hypothesis and target metric, plus a RankBreeze "track a change" entry.
4. Measure at 14 and 30 days: the targeted funnel metric vs similar listings, and vs before.

chunks.heading: Cadence
chunks.text:
- Launch report on day 3–5.
- Day-30 funnel re-check.
- Re-audit quarterly, or when the pickup watch flags a listing.

chunks.heading: Open questions (Fede)
chunks.text:
- RankBreeze plan coverage for all client listings, and whether there is an API or export, or whether the agent reads it in the browser.
- Should the funnel table be page 1 of the launch report?

# Needs Listing Review (post-call option 4)

**Status: draft, proposed 2026-10-08. Not yet approved by Fede.** First case: [[audits/needs-listing-review-teresa-le-2026-10-08]].

- Owner: the closer owns the lead and the follow-up. Fede signs off on the analysis. The builder is not on file yet (proposed: Andrés, with Gaston for Hub pulls).
- When to use: after a discovery call, the closer sets GHL `RF Post-Call Outcome` to `4 — Needs listing review` because the prospect wants evidence before signing.
- Turnaround: whatever the closer promised on the call (Teresa: 2 days). Default: 2 business days from the call.

chunks.heading: What we have today (2026-10-08)
chunks.text:
- Setting option 4 fires a GHL workflow that sends one generic email, "Send us your listings for review". It asks for up to 3 listing links and the client's questions by reply.
- It does **not** create a task, assign an owner, move the opportunity, remind the client, or notify the team. The Hub intake (`/listing-review/<token>`, migration 090, decision 2026-08-30 in the Hub repo) exists but is not connected to it.

chunks.heading: The analysis: two parts
chunks.text: Prospects ask two different questions. Answer both.

chunks.heading: A. "How does my listing compare to the market?" (their comps)
chunks.text:
1. **Pin the property:** exact address, bedrooms/baths, sleeps, key amenities (hot tub, sauna, view, pool), and the Airbnb link. Write the address back to GHL `RF Property Address`.
2. **Their actuals,** best source first: PriceLabs access (many prospects already use it; add our access identity, see [[decisions/2026-07-01-revfactor-access-identities]]), then a PMS export (12 months of reservations), then a Rankbreeze/AirROI estimate scraped from the public calendar. Label which one we used.
3. **Comp set:** follow [[playbooks/comp-analysis]] (fit + competitive tier + performance; no mid-term rentals, no zombies). Aim for 8–15 accepted listings in the same submarket, same bedroom count (±1 only as a size view), same amenity class. Use the PriceLabs Market Dashboard (custom map area plus filters) or the Rankbreeze Listing Review export. The `revfactor-listing-review` skill digests the Rankbreeze file.
4. **Table:** trailing 12 months and next 90 days (pacing) for ADR, occupancy and RevPAR, listing vs comp median and 75th percentile, plus RevPAR index.
5. **2–4 specific opportunities** tied to the numbers (examples: weekday occupancy gap, under-priced holiday peak, far-out dates too cheap, min-stay blocking orphan nights). Revenue advice only; no purchase advice.

chunks.heading: B. "Show me RevFactor works on a property like mine" (our proof)
chunks.text:
1. Pull managed listings in the same market from the Hub: `report_listings` joined to `report_metrics` (latest completed `report_runs`), filtered by city and bedroom count.
2. **Lead with market-normalized numbers:** RevPAR index (listing RevPAR ÷ market RevPAR) before vs after the setup date (`listings.initial_setup_date`). Raw year-over-year revenue misleads when the listing was already growing.
3. Anonymize: no owner name, listing title or exact location in anything sent to a prospect. Say, for example, "1BR hot-tub cabin, Sevierville".
4. Mark forward months as "on the books as of <report date>", not results.
5. If no managed listing matches on bedrooms, say so and show the closest ones. Never invent a comparable.

chunks.heading: Estimate format (new or pre-launch listings; Fede, 2026-10-09)
chunks.text:
- **Three comp levels, each shown at the 50th / 75th / 90th percentile:**
  - Conservative: same bedroom count.
  - Base: one bedroom count up, when capacity justifies it.
  - Strong: premium amenity peers.
  - Annual = listed nightly rate × that level's occupancy × 365.
- Place the property by quality. Professional design and photos (e.g. Somerled) put it at the 75th–90th percentile.
- **Year 1: always point the client to Conservative.** Everything above is upside as reviews build.
- When comparing across bedroom counts, add the caveat that it's "a bit nuanced": larger groups often filter by bedroom count first, so the larger-bedroom levels are possible, not expected.
- Tie it to our results in the same market (median RevPAR vs market, before/after, one anonymized top performer), stating how many listings it covers.
- Place outside estimates (another manager's figure) on this scale. Never reverse-engineer to hit them.
- First case: Jen MacDonald, Pigeon Forge 3BR that sleeps 13 (via Ethan, 2026-10-09).

chunks.heading: Deliverable
chunks.text:
- One page (PDF or email): A's table and opportunities, B's 1–3 anonymized proof cards, and the offer and next step (onboarding link). Fede approves before the closer sends it.
- Log it on the GHL opportunity as a note, and add a dated row to the audit.

chunks.heading: Proposed workflow v2 (needs Fede's approval; GHL is production)
chunks.text:
On `RF Post-Call Outcome = 4`:
1. Move the opportunity to a new **Listing Review** stage, or tag `needs-listing-review`.
2. Create GHL tasks: one for the closer (send analysis, due +2 business days) and one for the builder (pull comps, due +1).
3. Send an internal alert (Slack `#revfactor-sales`) with the contact, listing link and closer.
4. Rewrite the prospect email so it asks for what the analysis needs: exact address, PriceLabs access *or* a 12-month export, and goals. Ideally it links to the Hub intake instead of "reply".
5. Reminder at 48h if `RF Listings Submitted` is empty.

chunks.heading: Do not
chunks.text:
- Don't send owner names, listing titles or revenue of managed clients to a prospect.
- Don't quote unverified claims ("18–35% lift", "300+ listings"); see [[funnel/sales-funnel]].
- Don't publish or change the GHL workflow without Fede's explicit OK.

# Onboarding v2 (draft for the build)

Status: draft, 2026-10-12. Built from [[audits/onboarding-journey-2026-10-12]]. This replaces [[playbooks/onboarding]] once Fede approves it.

chunks.heading: Decisions (Fede, 2026-10-12)
chunks.text:
- **Fede runs every onboarding call.**
- **The Spencer pilot is the target flow.** The plan is to replace the India setup team over time with AI (agents plus the Grok bot) and internal employees. During the transition, India is a fallback that executes approved specs only.
- **GHL is the source of truth for intake.** Build on the current GHL fields and the `revfactor_listings` custom object; the Hub mirrors them. After each call, Fede's Granola notes are the second input.
- **The listing audit becomes a deliverable in the first days** instead of something promised before or on the call. Nobody was preparing it before the call, so it moves after the call.

chunks.heading: Ontology (RevFactor framework, applies to everything here)
chunks.text:
- **Anchor:** the Listing (canonical Airbnb ID). Everything links to a Listing and/or a Client plus an action.
- **Objects:** OnboardingRun, OwnerGoal (per listing: break-even, goal, floor basis, min-stay rules, owner blocks), AccessCheck, SetupSpec, ListingReview, LaunchReport, Adjustment.
- **Actions** (each with caller, tier, audit row, undo): SubmitIntake (client), RecordCallNotes (agent from Granola, Fede approves), VerifyAccess (ops), DraftSetupSpec (agent), ApproveSetupSpec (Fede), ApplySetup (ops), StampGoLive (system on first push), SubmitListingReviewDraft / PublishListingReview / DecideSuggestion (see [[playbooks/listing-optimization]]), SendLaunchReport (ops).
- **Exceptions** (one queue): access not verified by day 4; goal above market support; break-even above market; no booking 7 days after go-live; pace below target curve; setup corrected within 14 days; owner decisions pending 7 days.
- **Chain:** Exception → Recommendation → Decision → Execution → Outcome. Outcomes: pace vs target at days 14 and 30, RevPAR index vs comps and STLY, day-30 re-audit of the listing review.
- **Numbers come from code** (targets, scores, pace). AI writes wording only.
- Hub mapping: `docs/ontology/listing-review.md` (branch feat/listing-optimization-portal); folds into RM `docs/ontology.md`.

chunks.heading: Onboarding call script (45 min)
chunks.text:
1. **Access (15 min). Finish it on the call, don't leave it for later:** Airbnb co-host → PMS user → PriceLabs (check what's connected, send the transfer email) → Vrbo / Booking 2FA → portal magic link.
2. **Economics and rules (15 min).** Confirm the form answers per listing: break-even (amount + period + what it covers), owner goal, floor (payout or guest price), 1-night and min-stay rules, owner blocks, events, priority (rate / occupancy / reviews), who decides on price.
3. **Goal vs market (5 min).** Show the prep-pack market support. Agree the year-1 target (conservative level). If goal > market, say so now.
4. **Expectations (5 min), same words every time:** setup in 2–5 days, launch report by day 5, first monthly report at day 30, portal Mon–Fri with a ~24 h reply, what success looks like in the first 30/60/90 days.
5. **Scope (2 min):** what's included and what isn't. Extras (direct site, channel builds, PMS setup) get logged as offers, not done ad hoc.
6. **Open questions → tasks** before hanging up.

chunks.heading: GHL onboarding form changes
chunks.text:
Fields marked "exists" are already on the `revfactor_listings` custom object or the contact; they only need to be put on the form.

**Per listing (required):**
- Airbnb URL *(exists)*
- Live or launch date *(exists: listing_status, launch_date)*
- Annual revenue goal and where it comes from *(exists: annual_revenue_target; source: reuse the MC Revenue Expectation Source options)*
- **Break-even: amount + period (month/year) + what it covers (mortgage, cleaning, utilities, management)** *(new; replaces the "do you know it?" question)*
- Minimum nightly price *(exists)* + **is that your payout or the guest price?** *(new)*
- Guest cleaning fee *(new)* and turnover cost *(exists: cleaning_cost)*
- Minimum stay midweek / weekend *(exists)*, **no default values**, + **are 1-night stays allowed?** (never / gap nights only / yes) *(new)*
- **Owner blocks: date ranges** *(new structured field; today only free text in rf_v1_restriction_details)*

**Per listing (required, new):** "Has anything changed in the last 24 months?" Checkboxes: renovation or furniture, amenity added or removed, bedrooms or capacity, new photos, new listing, was long-term rented, seasonal or permit limits, was self-managed or with another manager. Each has a month/year and a note. This feeds ListingStage and ListingChange ([[playbooks/goals-and-targets]]).

**Per listing (optional):** events *(exists)*, comps *(exists)*, main goal *(exists: rf_v1_main_goal)*, rules we must not change *(exists: rf_v1_pricing_restrictions)*.

**Per client (new):**
- Who has final say on pricing
- Report recipients and channel
- Other channels in use (Vrbo / Booking / direct)
- Permit or night caps

**Remove:** `audit_requested`, because the audit is now standard for every client.

Mirror: GHL → Hub goals record per listing, which feeds the setup spec and the targets. See the goals framework in [[playbooks/comp-analysis]].

chunks.heading: Launch report (audit deliverable) contents
chunks.text:
1. Listing audit: the 16-dimension rubric from the existing airbnb-audit skill, scored, plus the top 5 listing fixes.
2. Account check: reviews and responses, Superhost / Guest Favorite, Instant Book, cancellation policy, other listings on the account.
3. Market position: comp tier, market support at P50/P75/P90, where our target sits.
4. What we set and why: base / floor / max, min stays, gap rule, far-out, last-minute, discounts and markups (payout math).
5. Targets: year-1 revenue target, monthly targets, pace expectations.
6. What happens next: day 14 check-in, day 30 report.

The skill that produces this is step 2 of the walkthrough.
