# Setup spec (draft)

Status: draft, 2026-10-13. Fede answered the first open questions on 2026-10-13 (see Decided, at the bottom). Part of [[playbooks/onboarding-v2]] (days 2–5). Inputs come from [[playbooks/goals-and-targets]]. Ontology: [[ontology/listing-review-and-onboarding]] (object **SetupSpec**).

chunks.heading: Why
chunks.text:
The first pricing setup is where onboarding breaks most ([[audits/onboarding-journey-2026-10-12]], stages 7–10):
- There is no template. 22 of 58 setup briefs were empty, and the median brief was 53 characters long. Only 6 mentioned a goal and 4 a floor. Several were briefed by analogy ("similar to Fools Gold").
- There is no QA gate. "Controlled" is a click, a median of 46 hours after the work and often in batches. 19% of setups were corrected within 14 days and 34% within 30, and clients found most of the errors.
- Go-live is not recorded. `live_at` is empty on every run, so day 14, 30 and 90 can't be computed.

The Spencer pilot (Fede's own day 1–5 flow) is the target. To replace India with agents and internal staff, the setup has to be a spec that code fills in and a person approves, not a free-text brief.

chunks.heading: What a setup spec is
Inputs (all required before drafting)
chunks.text:
| Input | From | Blocks the draft if missing |
|---|---|---|
| Goals record: break-even (amount, period, includes), owner goal, floor and its basis, min-stay and 1-night rules, owner blocks, events, priority | GHL form + call notes ([[playbooks/goals-and-targets]]) | Yes, raise `floor_basis_unknown` |
| Listing stage (new / changed / established) and material changes | ClassifyListingStage, ListingChange | Yes |
| Market support P50 / P75 / P90 by month, comp tier and comp set | ComputeMarketSupport ([[skills/comp-analysis]]) | Yes |
| Approved base target and monthly targets | ApproveTargets | Yes. A setup without targets is a guess. |
| Channels and PMS: which channels, which PMS, who controls markups and promotions | Access gate ([[playbooks/onboarding-v2]]) | Yes |
| Costs: guest cleaning fee, turnover cost, taxes set up (pass-through or not) | GHL form, [[skills/taxes-pass-through]], [[skills/international-taxes]] | Yes for the floor math |
| Listing review findings (instant book, cancellation policy, capacity) | [[playbooks/listing-optimization]] | No. Owner choices stay with the owner. |

chunks.heading: The spec, section by section
chunks.text: Each section says how the value is computed and which rule or skill it comes from. "Default" values are what the agent drafts; Fede can change any of them on approval.

chunks.heading: 1. Base price
chunks.text:
- **Base** = the approved base target's ADR for the listing's tier, from market support ([[playbooks/goals-and-targets]]: Standard P50→P75, Strong P75→P90, Premium P90→top). Not the owner's past ADR and not the owner goal.
- **Stage adjustments:**
  - New listing: penetration pricing for the first 30–60 calendar days to win bookings and reviews, plus the launch markup (+20% from day 1, 10% after 30 days out, off after the first 3 bookings) ([[skills/new-listing-launch]], [[decisions/2026-06-11-new-listing-launch-markup]]).
  - Changed: base from post-change data if there are enough months, otherwise market support.
  - Established: base from the listing's RevPAR index vs the market, never from raw past dollars.
- **Check:** the seasonal rates times the expected booked nights must land within ±10% of the approved annual target. If not, the spec says why (owner blocks, permit cap, ramp).

chunks.heading: 2. Floor (PriceLabs minimum price)
chunks.text:
- **Floor payout per night** = the higher of break-even per available night and the owner's "never below" price, both as **payout after channel fees**, excluding the cleaning fee (charged separately). Decided by Fede, 2026-10-13 (goals question 5).
- **PriceLabs minimum** = floor payout ÷ the lowest payout share the listing can hit on any channel. The payout share is (1 + channel markup) × (1 − deepest discount that can apply) × (1 − top-rated-guest discount, if on) × (1 − host channel fee).
  - Worked example (Airbnb, 55% markup, top-rated on, monthly 28% is the deepest): 1.55 × 0.72 × 0.85 = 0.949 of the PriceLabs price before the host fee. With a $300 floor payout and a 15.5% host fee: 300 ÷ (0.949 × 0.845) ≈ **$374** PriceLabs minimum.
  - The host fee and markup come from the live PMS and channel settings, never assumed ([[skills/ota-markup]]).
- **Per season** if the owner gave seasonal floors (Spencer: Mount Washington $600, $550 in winter; Horse Farm $900). Review each season ([[skills/minimum-price-floor]]).
- Protect it with PriceLabs' safety minimum price.
- Gap-night and last-minute discounts can reach the floor. Check them together.

chunks.heading: 3. Maximum price
chunks.text:
- **Default:** max = 3× base, plus date-specific overrides for known events (Fede, 2026-10-13).
- Events: open high early, then walk toward the target as the booking window develops. Pace triggers changes, not the event itself ([[skills/event-pricing]]). Spencer's Derby bookings historically land around November.

chunks.heading: 4. Minimum stay
chunks.text:
- **Owner rule first.** The goals record wins: midweek and weekend minimums and the 1-night policy (never / gap nights only / yes). No default values on the form.
- **Default profile** when the owner has no preference: 2 nights base, 3 on weekends, holidays and high season.
- **Day-of-week check:** a Thursday or Sunday minimum that strands nights next to a weekend is a defect (Salt & Sol: treat Thursday as a weekend night).
- **Far-out minimums by season:** higher minimums far out in strong months, competitive in slow months. No blanket far-out premium.
- **Cleaning cost check:** if the turnover cost is higher than the guest cleaning fee, short stays can lose money. The minimum stay or the gap premium must cover the difference.
- Spencer pilot: flexible 2–3 night stays replaced the prior manager's 5-night minimum (Mount Washington 2, Horse Farm 3).

chunks.heading: 5. Gap (orphan) nights
chunks.text:
- Short stays only to fill gaps, never opened generally, unless the owner allows 1-night stays.
- **Default gap premium:** +15% on 1-night gaps (Fede, 2026-10-13). Go higher only where cleaning costs require it, and record the reason on the spec.
- Confirm the orphan-night setting explicitly on every listing. It is a QA item.

chunks.heading: 6. Seasonality, far-out and last-minute
chunks.text:
- **Seasonal profiles** from the monthly targets: peak months protected, slow months competitive. Use last year's **market** pacing, not the owner's ([[skills/no-history-pricing]]).
- **Far-out:** premium on peak-season dates only, set by season.
- **Last-minute:** gradual decrease inside the booking window, stopping at the floor. Airbnb's own last-minute discount (20%, 0–28 days) sits on top. Only one of length-of-stay, early bird or last minute applies per booking ([[skills/channel-discounts]]).

chunks.heading: 7. Day of week
chunks.text:
- Weekend premium from the comp set's weekend/weekday spread. Default: PriceLabs' market DOW unless the comps disagree by more than 10 points.
- Prefer length-of-stay discounts over rigid minimums to win longer stays.

chunks.heading: 8. Channels: markups, discounts and promotions
chunks.text:
- **Airbnb markup** 44% without the top-rated-guest discount, 55% with it ([[skills/ota-markup]]). The top-rated discount is a per-listing choice. Default it on for listings coming out of slow bookings.
- **Airbnb discounts** (Fede's defaults, 2026-10-09): trip length 21/22/26% (3+/5+/14+ nights), weekly 24%, monthly 28%, early bird 20%, last minute 20% ([[skills/channel-discounts]]).
- **Vrbo:** markup per listing (Spencer 12%), slightly above Airbnb. Opt out of Members Only Deals. Vrbo can't use Airbnb-style early bird, last-minute or trip-length discounts.
- **Booking.com and direct are in scope for the first setup** (Fede, 2026-10-13).
- **Direct is always the cheapest guest total.** Owners always want direct below Airbnb (Fede, 2026-10-13). Compare the guest's checkout total for the same dates, guests and length of stay, not the nightly rate.
  - **Direct** = the PriceLabs target. The direct site copies Airbnb's length-of-stay discounts (trip length, weekly, monthly) (Fede, 2026-10-13), and its discounts must at least match Airbnb's deepest stack for the same stay length. Otherwise a long Airbnb stay can undercut direct: with a 55% markup, the monthly 28% plus the top-rated 15% lands at $94.86 on a $100 target (see [[skills/explain-markups-and-discounts]]).
  - **Vrbo** about 5% above direct (Granola a53950b0, 2026-09-29), set per listing. Spencer: 12%.
  - **Booking.com:** the markup covers the property's contracted commission and keeps the guest total above direct. Default: commission + 5 points (Fede, 2026-10-13). Use the real commission from the contract, never an assumed one.
  - **Airbnb** stays above direct through the 44% or 55% markup.
  - Recheck the totals whenever cleaning fees, taxes, promotions or commission terms change.
- Every channel row says **where the setting lives** (PriceLabs, PMS, channel dashboard) and who controls it.

chunks.heading: 9. Taxes and fees
chunks.text:
- Pass-through taxes set up where needed ([[skills/taxes-pass-through]]). International withholding per [[skills/international-taxes]].
- Guest cleaning fee as the owner set it. If it is out of line with comps, raise it with the owner; we don't change it.

chunks.heading: 10. Blocks and calendar
chunks.text:
- Owner blocks entered as date ranges from the goals record.
- Calendar open window: default 12 months. A blocked calendar stops prices from pushing (Florence, Lake Como).
- Permit or night caps (e.g. a 120-night limit) recorded with how they are enforced.

chunks.heading: 11. Child listings
chunks.text: Only for extra units, never for one home on two channels ([[skills/child-listing-pricing]], [[playbooks/pricelabs-transfer]]).

chunks.heading: QA gate (before sync goes on)
chunks.text:
Run by the ops agent against the **live** settings, not the spec. Every item is pass / fail / n/a. Sync stays off until every item passes or Fede or Gaston waives it with a reason.

| # | Check | Compares |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | PriceLabs is the only pricing engine; PMS dynamic pricing is off | PMS settings |
| 2 | Listing and channel mapping are correct (right PriceLabs id ↔ Hub listing ↔ Airbnb ID) | PriceLabs, Hub |
| 3 | Base, min and max match the spec | PriceLabs |
| 4 | Lowest possible payout ≥ floor payout, on every channel, with every discount stack | Computed from live markup and discounts |
| 5 | Min-stay profile matches the owner rule, including DOW and far-out | PriceLabs |
| 6 | Orphan-night rule set and matches the spec | PriceLabs |
| 7 | Owner blocks are in | Channel calendar |
| 8 | Markups set on every channel | PMS |
| 9 | Discounts and promotions match the spec; Vrbo Members Only Deals off | Channel dashboards |
| 10 | Taxes and fees set; the guest total on a test stay looks right | Channel checkout preview |
| 11 | Calendar open to the agreed window; no stray blocks | Channel calendar |
| 12 | Sample prices: next 30 days and the peak month show plausible guest totals vs comps | PriceLabs calendar vs comps |
| 13 | Direct is the cheapest guest total on every channel for 2, 3, 7 and 30-night test stays, including the deepest Airbnb stack | Checkout totals on each channel and the direct site |

Any failure becomes an Adjustment against the setup, assigned to the applier. Record the result on the spec: who ran it, when, and every item's status.

chunks.heading: Go-live
chunks.text:
- **StampGoLive** at the first successful price push after the QA gate passes: `live_at` on the listing. Day 0 for the pickup watch, the day-14 check-in and the day-30 report.
- Turning sync on before the QA gate passes is itself an exception (Mark and Patricia went live early).

chunks.heading: Ontology
chunks.text:
- **Object: SetupSpec** (per listing, versioned), linked to Listing, Client, OwnerGoal and the setup Adjustment.
  - Fields: one row per setting (value, unit, where it lives, the rule or skill it came from, the reason); inputs snapshot (goals record version, comps and market support at drafting, stage); status (draft → approved → applied → QA passed → live); approved by and when; applied by and when; QA result per check; revisions with reasons.
- **Actions:**

  | Action | Who | Approval | Audit |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | DraftSetupSpec | ops agent (code computes, AI writes reasons) | none (draft) | event row |
  | ApproveSetupSpec | Fede, on every spec | Fede | event row, approved version frozen |
  | ApplySetup | ops employee or India | needs an approved spec | event row per setting group |
  | ReviseSetupSpec | applier proposes, Fede approves | Fede | append-only, with reason |
  | RunSetupQA | ops agent | — | QA result row |
  | WaiveQACheck | Fede or Gaston | Fede or Gaston | event row with reason |
  | StampGoLive | system at the first push | — | `live_at` |

- **Exceptions:**
  - `setup_inputs_missing`: a draft is blocked on a missing input (names which).
  - `spec_unapproved_48h`: drafted and waiting on Fede.
  - `applied_not_qa_24h`: applied, QA not run.
  - `qa_failed`: one per failed check.
  - `direct_not_cheapest`: a channel's guest total is at or below direct for a test stay.
  - `live_before_qa`: prices pushing with the QA gate not passed.
  - `setup_drift`: a live setting no longer matches the approved spec with no revision (a weekly diff).
  - `setup_corrected_14d`: a setting corrected within 14 days of go-live. This is the quality metric for the spec itself.
- **Chain:** the setup exception (no spec, QA failed, drift) → recommendation (the draft spec or the revision) → decision (Fede's approval) → execution (ApplySetup, then the QA gate passing) → outcome (no correction within 14 days; pace vs the target curve at days 14 and 30).
- **Numbers come from code:** floor math, payout shares, base from market support, QA comparisons. AI writes only each setting's reason and the owner-facing summary in the launch report.

chunks.heading: Outputs
chunks.text:
- The approved spec is the "what we set and why" section of the launch report ([[playbooks/onboarding-v2]]).
- The spec's settings are the baseline for the day-30 review and for `setup_drift`.
- Success measure: the 14-day correction rate drops from 19% toward 0, and no client finds a setup error before we do.

chunks.heading: Transition with India
chunks.text: India gets the approved spec, not a brief. They apply it exactly, mark each setting group done, and request a revision instead of improvising. The QA gate is run by us, not by them.

chunks.text:
1. **Floor:** break-even payout after channel fees, excluding cleaning, with the owner's "never below" price on top.
2. **Max price:** 3× base, plus event overrides.
3. **Gap premium:** +15%.
4. **QA waivers:** Fede or Gaston.
5. **Approval:** Fede approves every spec.
6. **Booking.com and direct:** in scope for the first setup. Direct is always the cheapest guest total.
7. **Booking.com markup:** its contracted commission + 5 points.
8. **Direct-site discounts:** copy Airbnb's length-of-stay discounts.

# Support ticket flow

- Assembly message → support capture bot → `POST /api/v1/support-captures` on the Hub (contract v1.4, 2026-10-01; endpoints live 2026-09-30).
- The bot reads the client's open tickets and listings first, processes one client at a time in order, and sends one capture per message: new asks become tickets, follow-ups become events on existing tickets, unsure cases go to triage.
- The Hub decides status, priority, owner, overdue and chases. Promises (including hedged ones) become commitments. Money-at-stake tickets need a pass to be marked answered.
- The bot may store one draft reply per ticket; a person always sends.
- Status 2026-10-01: test mode; no live clients; Hub `support_tickets` is empty. A dry-run backfill exists (`/workspace/support-bot/`).
- Sources: revfactor-hub `docs/support/capture-bot-contract.md`; `/workspace/support-bot/README.md`.

# Client communication

- Clients talk to us in their Assembly chat ([[stack/assembly]]). A human sends every message; bots draft only (`/workspace/revfactor-role-cards.md`).
- Andrés is the default sender; Fede and Gaston handle strategy and material exceptions.
- Portal-only after signing; no strategy calls by default (`/workspace/revfactor-onboarding-map.md`).
- Revenue advice only. Purchase or property questions get revenue estimates; the client decides. No guarantees, no single magic number.
- Promises made in chat are tracked as commitments on Hub Support tickets ([[playbooks/support-ticket-flow]]).

chunks.text:
Summaries of cited sources, not yet reviewed.
- **Response target:** 24 hours on business days, agreed with a client on 2026-09-29 (Granola a53950b0). A client called 24-hour replies too slow for dynamic pricing (Granola e46b8173 2026-07-01). On 2026-09-28, items had gone silent for 7–27 days (Slack #revfactor-main-chat).
- **No ad hoc calls; questions in writing.** Restated 2026-08-26 (Granola 7b5cd12c), with a portal message saying the service does not include strategy calls (Slack 2026-08-26). Exceptions do happen: Fede held review calls with unhappy clients (Granola e46b8173 2026-07-01; a53950b0 2026-09-29).
- **Portal is the channel.** Sales discourages direct email from clients (Slack #revfactor-sales 2026-09-22). The portal moved to owner.revfactor.io (Gmail 2026-10-01).
- **Proactive updates wanted.** Clients ask for automated performance emails and for reports that include a plan (Gmail 2026-10-01; Slack 2026-09-29). Weekly reports planned (Granola a53950b0).
- **Unanswered messages:** after a weekend message went unanswered and delayed an onboarding, the team decided on a daily end-of-day chat review and a bot that flags unanswered Assembly messages (Granola 7b5cd12c 2026-08-26).

- Request rules are in [[policies/client-requests]].

# Client requests: verify, explain, decide

Evidence v2. This collects the request rules stated in meetings and Slack. Not yet reviewed as policy.

chunks.heading: The rule
chunks.text:
1. **Verify:** check market position, comps and where rates stand before changing anything.
2. **Explain:** send the client the context for why rates are set as they are.
3. **Decide:** accept or decline only after the analysis.
(Granola abfed974 2026-07-03, decided after the India team said yes to every request without analysis.)

chunks.heading: Two kinds of questions
chunks.text:
- **Operational** (block dates, minimum stay, discount rules): answer fast; a bot may answer first.
- **Strategic** (pricing analysis, event markup, underperformance): human-reviewed, with analysis attached. (Granola abfed974 2026-07-03)

chunks.heading: Pushback
chunks.text:
- Defend the position with data and set a review date, for example: "let's review ADR, occupancy and RevPAR against market after X days" (Granola ffc41f83 2026-06-11).
- After any change, check it in Airbnb's guest view and send a screenshot. Explain that the host calendar shows the price before discounts and the guest sees it after (Granola ffc41f83).
- Acknowledging and resolving are separate: acknowledge at once even when the fix takes longer (Granola ffc41f83).

chunks.heading: Early warning signs of an unhappy client
What a reply must contain
chunks.text:
- An answer to the exact question. A yes or no gets a yes or no, not statistics (Slack 2026-09-28).
- Reports must say what we will do, not only what is wrong (client feedback, Slack 2026-09-29).
- Close the loop: confirm that the change was made. Twelve "did we actually do it?" checks were open on 2026-09-28 (Slack #revfactor-main-chat).

chunks.heading: Who decides
chunks.text:
- Money (refunds, disputed charges, waivers): Fede or Gaston (Slack 2026-09-28).
- Report and performance replies: Fede reviews before sending, from 2026-09-29 (Slack #revfactor-main-chat).
- Listing changes for a new high-touch client: none without Fede (v1 Notion board, see the client page).

# Client contract and pricing

chunks.heading: Signed contract on file: "Small Portfolio Plan · 1 to 5 Properties"
chunks.text:
Revenue Management Service Agreement between RevFactorio LLC and the client (Texas law). Example on file signed 2026-04-10 (`/workspace/RevFactor-Contract-1-5.txt`).

- **Scope:** pricing strategy and dynamic rates, market and competitor tracking, listing optimization recommendations, fee and minimum-stay strategy, trend and event tracking, monthly performance updates, shared performance dashboard (view only), support through the owner portal (Assembly).
- **Price:** $320 / month for 1 property; $304 each for 2; $288 each for 3; $272 each for 4; $256 each for 5. Onboarding fee $125 one-time, paid manually before service starts. Child listings $35 per child per month.
- **Billing:** invoiced at the start of each month; 7-day grace; $25 late fee after grace; non-payment past 15 days may suspend or end service; declined autopay must be fixed within 3 business days. Recurring charges go through Stripe.
- **Term:** 3-month initial commitment, then month-to-month with 30 days' written notice. Early exit inside the first 3 months owes 100% of the remaining commitment.
- **Client duties:** onboarding form and access (Airbnb, Vrbo, PriceLabs, PMS); share goals, past P&L and market insight; answer requests in time; do not change settings or prices without RevFactor's approval.
- **No revenue guarantee.** Performance Review can be requested after 120 days of continuous service (YoY revenue and occupancy, RevPAR, market penetration, ADR vs market, event uplift, booking window). If performance did not improve, the property underperformed the market and the client implemented all major recommendations, the client may leave without the early-exit fee. It does not apply when the client delayed recommendations, changed settings, gave late access, the property had unusual issues, it is a first-time listing, or the market fell.
- **Confidentiality:** clients must not share our tools, dashboards, SOPs or strategy docs.

chunks.heading: Current pricing for new signups (GHL native flow)
chunks.text: Notion "RF onboarding reference — Native signup, Live agreements and pricing" (2026-09-12): $350 per primary listing per month, $50 per child listing per month, $150 one-time onboarding fee, 1–5 primary listings via `start.revfactor.io`.

chunks.heading: Conflict
chunks.text: Child listing price ($35 vs $50), onboarding fee ($125 vs $150) and base price ($320 tiers vs $350) differ between the signed contract and the new GHL flow. Live book is mixed ($320 majority, some $350). Each client's actual price is on their page from Stripe. Logged in [[audits/spine-2026-10-01]].

- No passwords, logins, one-time codes, API keys, tokens or card numbers in this vault, commits or PR text. Write "in Hub credentials" (Hub `client_credentials`).
- `tools/brain/check_vault.py` runs a secrets scan; it must pass before any merge.

# Launch and listing pricing rules

Evidence v2. These are revenue-management rules the team stated in meetings. They are revenue advice only.

chunks.heading: New listing launch
chunks.text:
- The listing must be 100% ready, with professional photos, before going live (Granola ffc41f83 2026-06-11; fd8d6a85 2026-06-09).
- Price competitively for the first 30–60 calendar days to win bookings and reviews; far-out dates can carry a premium (Granola ffc41f83; 9bf38589 2026-07-16; ac1c2c17 2026-08-20).
- Airbnb gives new listings a 20% discount for the first guests. Mark base rates up 20% first, drop to 10% after 30 days out, and remove the markup after the first 3 bookings. **Team decision 2026-06-11:** the markup applies from day 1 on every new listing ([[decisions/2026-06-11-new-listing-launch-markup]]).
- One client opened 45 days out at a 20% discount to avoid locking in low holiday rates (Granola 7aab0b9f 2026-08-25).

chunks.heading: Properties without booking history
chunks.text:
- The India team's 20% safety buffer against last year works only when there is history. A standard for listings without history was raised 3+ times over 6 weeks without a fix (Granola 5a4edf7e 2026-07-01).
- Price new or renovated properties to market potential, not to the owner's prior-year numbers. Use last year's **market** pacing, not the owner's pacing (Granola 6be61332 2026-07-01).
- Each property needs a 12-month revenue target split by month. Run quarterly pacing reviews and flag properties 15–20% behind (Granola 6be61332).

chunks.heading: Child listings
chunks.text:
- Keep the child closed in high season with doubled rates, a 7-night minimum and blocks. Price it about 30% under the parent further out and more aggressively at the last minute (Granola ac1c2c17 2026-08-20; 9f4178d6 2026-08-20).
- A child priced above its parent caused a near-cancellation (Granola abfed974 2026-07-03).

chunks.heading: Comps
chunks.text:
- Use two comp types: apples-to-apples (same quality) and next-best alternative (what the guest substitutes). Airbnb's "similar listings" shows what Airbnb treats as comps (Granola ffc41f83).
- AirDNA Rentalizer is a market reference, not a ceiling (Slack 2026-08-24).

chunks.heading: Discounts defaults noted (private note, 2026-09-10)
chunks.text: Weekly 25%, monthly 28%, early bird 20% (1 month+), last minute 20% (0–28 days). (Granola 1c97175c) Treat these as notes, not as approved policy.

chunks.heading: Airbnb top-rated-guest discount
chunks.text: An opt-in 15% that stacks on other discounts. Opt in selectively and adjust base pricing for the stack (Granola ad2ebf1c 2026-07-27). Some clients refuse it and others want it only with a markup, so automation needs a per-client opt-out (Slack 2026-09-07).

# Adjustment flow (Hub)

How client change requests and internal fixes move today. Evidence: Hub tables pulled 2026-10-01 ([[evidence/hub-operations-2026-10-01]]) and meetings.

1. **Intake.** The request is logged as a Hub adjustment by the internal team (about 150), HostPricing (32), an agent (53) or the client (25). Each record has scope (single listing or portfolio), type, target value, dates, urgency and origin.
2. **Notify.** The adjustment tracker sends a WhatsApp notification to the India team (Granola abfed974 2026-07-03).
3. **Work.** Statuses are open → in_progress / needs_info → resolved. The India team makes the change in PriceLabs.
4. **Control.** A reviewer moves resolved → controlled (194 of 427 status changes). Records carry the resolver and reviewer.
5. **Close the loop with the client.** No status for this. "Did we actually do it?" checks with clients pile up (12 open on 2026-09-28, Slack), and one client asked about a markup 4 times.

# Client triage (how unanswered work is found today)

Evidence v2.
- **2026-09-28:** Fede posted a triage list of about 40 clients in four buckets: (1) reply tonight, the client wrote last; (2) promises we broke; (3) answered wrong or only halfway; (4) "did we actually do it?" checks. Gaston and Andrés closed most of bucket 4 the next morning and wrote status per item. (Slack #revfactor-main-chat 2026-09-28..29)
- **Performance-sensitive watch list** posted by Andrés (2026-09-03, 2026-08-24): clients worried about YoY results, profit after costs, or projections against the mortgage.
- **Hot-chat signals** to flag in real time: see [[policies/client-requests]].
- A Sage bot posts open-thread updates in `#revfactor-open-threads`; Gaston wants Sage to answer questions there (Slack #revfactor-cos 2026-09-02).

chunks.heading: Gap
chunks.text: The list was built by hand from chat reading. No Hub view shows "client wrote last", age, or promised-by date (the support tables are empty). See [[processes/_candidates]].

# Decision → outcome loop

Every pricing change gets checked at +7 and +30 days. We compare bookings picked up after the change with the same point last year. Pilot: [[audits/outcome-pilot-ali-dowden-2026-10-05]]. Template: `_templates/outcome-check.md`. Status: **draft, pilot only**. Fede decides whether to run it for all clients.

chunks.heading: What counts as a decision
chunks.text:
- A Hub `adjustments` row with a listing, a type and a status of `resolved` or `controlled`.
- "Applied at" = `resolved_at`. Use `controlled_at` only if `resolved_at` is empty.
- Types we can measure: `price`, `min_price`, `max_price`, `min_stay`, `discount`, `markup_fees`, `setup`.
- Types we cannot measure with bookings: `visibility`, `review`, `recommendation`, `other`. Log them; skip the numbers.
- An open adjustment has no outcome yet. Record its baseline only.

chunks.heading: What we measure
chunks.text:
For the affected listing and nights (`date_from` to `date_to`; if empty, the next 365 nights):
1. **Baseline**: revenue and nights on the books the day before the change.
2. **Pickup at +7 and +30**: revenue and nights booked after the change, for those nights.
3. **STLY**: the same, for the same nights 364 days earlier, as of the same dates 364 days earlier.
4. **Channel split**: OTA (Airbnb, Vrbo, Booking.com) vs `manual` (direct or owner-entered). Our prices drive OTA bookings. Direct rates may not come from PriceLabs.
5. **Now**: on the books today vs STLY, as a longer check.

Revenue rules are the owner report v5 rules ([[metrics/portfolio-metrics]]). They are pending Fede.

chunks.heading: How to read it
chunks.text:
- **Supports the change**: pickup at +30 is at or above STLY pickup, and ADR is at or above STLY ADR.
- **Against the change**: pickup at +30 is below half of STLY pickup, with no other reason.
- **Can't tell**: any of these. Fewer than 3 bookings in either period. Mostly direct bookings. A calendar or minimum-stay change in the same window. No history last year.
- One listing and one change is an anecdote. Pool many changes of the same type before drawing a rule.

chunks.heading: Outcome SQL (read-only)
chunks.text:
Set the four parameters in `p`. It returns baseline, +7, +30 and today, each with STLY.

```sql
with p as (select '<PriceLabs listing id>'::text lid, date '<applied date>' t0,
                  date '<date_from>' sf, date '<date_to>' st, date '<as-of date>' asof),
res as (select distinct on (r.reservation_key) r.* from pricelabs_reservations_cache r, p
        where r.listing_id = p.lid and r.booking_status = 'booked'),
n as (select r.booked_date, r.booking_channel ch, d::date night,
             r.rental_revenue / greatest(r.number_of_days, 1) rev
      from res r cross join lateral generate_series(r.check_in, r.check_out - 1, interval '1 day') d),
k as (select * from (values ('baseline', -1), ('t0+7', 7), ('t0+30', 30), ('now', null)) v(k, off))
select k.k,
  round(sum(n.rev) filter (where n.night between p.sf and p.st
        and n.booked_date <= coalesce(p.t0 + k.off, p.asof)), 2) otb_rev,
  count(*) filter (where n.night between p.sf and p.st
        and n.booked_date <= coalesce(p.t0 + k.off, p.asof)) otb_nights,
  round(sum(n.rev) filter (where n.night between p.sf - 364 and p.st - 364
        and n.booked_date <= coalesce(p.t0 + k.off, p.asof) - 364), 2) stly_rev,
  count(*) filter (where n.night between p.sf - 364 and p.st - 364
        and n.booked_date <= coalesce(p.t0 + k.off, p.asof) - 364) stly_nights
from k cross join p cross join n group by k.k, k.off order by k.off nulls last;
```

Pickup at +7 = (+7 row − baseline row). Same for +30.

chunks.heading: Known limits (from the pilot)
chunks.text:
- The Hub logs only some changes. Many promises in client chats never became adjustments.
- Many adjustments have no `date_from` / `date_to`. Then we cannot tell which nights to watch.
- `resolved_at` is when the team marked it done. It is not the PriceLabs change time. PriceLabs logs (`POST /v1/logs`) would give the real time.
- The STLY rule drops stays that were booked last year and later cancelled.
- The feed has no blocked nights. A calendar block looks like weak demand.
- Twin listings double-count unless only the Hub-mapped PriceLabs id is used.

chunks.heading: Next steps (proposed)
chunks.text:
1. Require listing, `date_from`, `date_to` and type on every pricing adjustment.
2. Add two read-only views in the Hub: `adjustment_outcome_7d` and `adjustment_outcome_30d`. Gaston to build. Not started.
3. Review pooled results monthly by type (for example all `min_stay` changes). Andrés to own.
4. Show the +30 result on the adjustment card. Close the loop with the client after that.

# Reporting and wins

Evidence v2.
- **HostPricing** (India team) sends weekly "Performance Update" reports by email to Fede, Gaston and Andrés, and opens Hub adjustments for listings that need review (Gmail 2026-09-23, 2026-09-30).
- **Client reports** are built on request, for example a YoY report with revenue and MPI (Slack 2026-09-29). A client objected that she has to request, read and then chase a report to get any action (Slack 2026-09-29).
- **PriceLabs report pipeline** (Hub `report_runs`): 78 of 138 runs failed and 5 have been stuck since Jul–Aug.
- **Deliverable model** (Granola bb5046da 2026-07-29): 1) strategy, a 2×2 of ADR against occupancy; 2) tactics, automated monthly reports such as a PriceLabs reservation export and booking-window breakdown; 3) communicating wins.
- **Wins:** the tracker refreshes about every 15 days and excludes listings without enough last-year data (Granola 9f4178d6 2026-08-20). The Hub generated 42 win messages, and 1 was marked shared.
- **Education:** clients repeatedly ask for a dashboard and funnel explainer video (Slack 2026-08-19, 2026-08-26; Granola 9bf38589 2026-07-16).
- **Wanted:** a monthly digest (Hub board, in progress), a revenue goal tracker (Hub, next), and automated performance emails (client ask, Gmail 2026-10-01).

# wikifactor
RevFactor company brain. Obsidian vault. Clients + listings. Not the Hub.

- Agents start at [[BRAIN]]. Humans start at [[HOME]].
- Plain markdown, readable by people and agents. Open the folder as an Obsidian vault.
- Rebuild generated hub pages: `python3 tools/brain/build_hubs.py`. Check the vault: `python3 tools/brain/check_vault.py` (broken links, missing ids, secrets scan).
- No passwords, codes, API keys or card numbers in this repo. Logins live in the Hub `client_credentials` table; pages say "in Hub credentials".

# Review queue: how it works

One file per open question where two sources disagree. The index is [[Review]] (generated; do not hand-edit).

- **Add an item:** copy `_templates/review-item.md` to `review/R-NNN-<slug>.md` with the next free number. Fill both claims with their sources.
- **Decide:** the person in `Decides` writes the outcome under `## Decision` and sets `Status: decided`. Fede has the final say.
- **Apply:** update the pages listed under "Pages to update". Add a `decisions/` file when the outcome is a company rule. Then set `Status: closed`.
- **Never** pick a winner silently on a knowledge page. Link the item instead.
- `Decides: data` means a data fix settles it. The named owner does the fix.

# R-016 Official revenue number

- Status: open
- Decides: Fede
- Type: metric
- Opened: 2026-10-05
- Source: [[audits/revenue-sources-2026-10-05]]; handoff question 2026-10-04

chunks.heading: Claim A
chunks.text: Revenue = `total_cost` on `pricelabs_reservations_bq`. Source: [[BRAIN]] source order, [[stack/hub]], [[stack/pricelabs]].

chunks.heading: Claim B
chunks.text: Revenue = `rental_revenue`. Source: Hub code (reservations page, Excel export); owner report v5 (spread over nights, status booked).

chunks.heading: Claim C
chunks.text: Revenue = PriceLabs Report Builder `report_metrics.rental_revenue`. Source: Hub Wins and listing dashboard.

chunks.heading: Evidence
chunks.text:
- Feed and Report Builder match within 2% on 277 of 299 listing-months (Sep 2026).

# Channel discounts and promotions

- Kind: rule
- Area: discounts
- Status: team decision — default discounts stated by Fede 2026-10-09 (pricing sheet); the Vrbo opt-out is approved in the Hub knowledge base
- Owner: Fede.
- Channels: Airbnb, Vrbo.
- Tools: PriceLabs, PMS, Airbnb and Vrbo dashboards.
- When to use: setting or reviewing stay-length discounts, Airbnb's top-rated-guest discount, or Vrbo promotions.
- Summary: Default Airbnb discounts are weekly 24%, monthly 28%, trip length 21–26%, early bird 20%, last minute 20%; the 15% top-rated-guest discount is a per-listing choice (encouraged after slow bookings, paired with a 55% markup); opt out of Vrbo Members Only Deals.

chunks.heading: Steps
chunks.text:
1. **Vrbo Members Only Deals** (host-funded 12–20%, stacked on weekly/monthly discounts from 2026-09-18): opt out. The control location depends on the setup (Vrbo direct, Hospitable, Hostaway).
2. **Airbnb top-rated-guest discount** (15%, guests rated 4.8+ with 3+ reviews): a per-listing choice. When we use it, the Airbnb markup is 55% instead of 44% ([[skills/ota-markup]]). We encourage it for listings coming out of slow bookings, for an extra exposure bump in Airbnb search (Fede, 2026-10-09; Spencer's two listings). Keep a per-client opt-out: some clients refuse it, others want it only with a markup.
3. **Default Airbnb discounts** (Fede's pricing sheet, 2026-10-09; set in PriceLabs):
   - Weekly (7+ nights) 24%; monthly (28+ nights) 28%.
   - Trip length: 3+ nights 21%, 5+ nights 22%, 14+ nights 26%.
   - Early bird (booked 1+ month ahead) 20%; last minute (0–28 days ahead) 20%.

chunks.heading: How Airbnb stacks them (checked 2026-10-09)
chunks.text:
- Only one of these applies to a reservation: new listing promotion, custom promotion, length of stay (weekly, monthly, trip length), early bird, last minute. Airbnb picks by priority in that order, not by size.
- The top-rated-guest discount (15%) is the one that adds on top of whichever applies; it is taken off the already-discounted price.
- A non-refundable discount, if offered, comes off last, after all other discounts.
- With our defaults, trip length starts at 3 nights (21%) and outranks early bird and last minute, so those two only reach stays under 3 nights.
- Common client question. Answer: "Only one of weekly, monthly, trip length, early bird or last minute applies, picked by Airbnb's order; the top-rated-guest discount is the only one that adds on top."

chunks.heading: Do not
chunks.text:
- Do not leave a promotion on that a client did not choose: log a client's choice to keep one in Assembly.
- Do not stack discounts without checking the effective nightly rate (see [[skills/ota-markup]]).

chunks.heading: Decided / open
chunks.text:
- Decided: default discounts and the two Airbnb markups, 44% without and 55% with the top-rated-guest discount (Fede, 2026-10-09). They replace the 2026-09-10 private-note figures (weekly was noted as 25%).
- Open: Fede's review of the page as a whole.

chunks.text:
# Comps with a different guest count

- Kind: framework
- Area: comps
- Status: stated in meetings — Fede's method across calls (2026-08 to 2026-10); flagged by Fede as very important 2026-10-09
- Owner: Fede.
- Channels: Airbnb first (search filters by party size); PriceLabs comp filters.
- Tools: Airbnb and PriceLabs comp filters (bedrooms, bathrooms, guests), RM comp scorecard, booking history by party size.
- When to use: any comp review, and whenever a client sends a comp that hosts a different number of guests than their listing.
- Summary: Compare against comps with the same real guest capacity first; a comp that hosts fewer or more guests is context, not a rate setter, because capacity changes who books, which searches it appears in, and the revenue tier.

chunks.heading: Steps
chunks.text:
1. Build tiers by capacity and layout: Tier 1 matches bedrooms, guest capacity, bed setup, layout, and indoor gathering space; Tier 2 keeps the rooms with different amenities; Tier 3 is market context ([[skills/comp-analysis]]; capacity within ±20%).
2. Filter comps by guest count in Airbnb or PriceLabs, and compare pacing and occupancy, not just the displayed nightly rate.
3. Treat a comp with a different guest count as context only. Ticket #12: the client's "best comp" is the same unit as hers, but it hosts 4 and hers hosts 6, so it sells to a different party size.
4. Price for the party size the listing actually books, not its maximum. In a Colorado case, pricing a home for 14 guests hurt ranking because real demand was 6–10 guests (guest avatar mismatch).
5. Set a different capacity's revenue target from comps at that capacity, not from a fixed amount per extra guest: a 7-guest home was estimated at about $70K a year, 14-guest comps at $90K–$150K, and an 8-guest comp with a sauna at about $99K. Check the permit or HOA occupancy limit before changing listed capacity.
6. Before setting extra-guest fees, look at booking history by party size and booking type to find the valuable group segments.

chunks.heading: Do not
chunks.text:
- Do not carry a comp's rate across capacities with a per-guest uplift.
- Do not assume a higher maximum occupancy is better.

chunks.heading: Decided / open
chunks.text: - Open: no standard capacity adjustment or extra-guest-fee rule is on file. Fede's message to Michelle on guest-count comps (2026-10-09) was not captured by the Hub: add it here.

# Event pricing (pace first)

- Kind: framework
- Area: events
- Status: design rule — 2026-10-08; RM event intelligence in pilot
- Owner: Fede.
- Channels: all.
- Tools: RM event intelligence (queue, listing Events tab, market map), forward pace snapshots.
- When to use: an event, holiday, or weather alert might move demand for a listing's dates.
- Summary: Pace is the trigger and the event is the explanation; raise rates only when forward pace confirms demand, and never raise rates on a weather alert.

chunks.heading: Steps
chunks.text:
1. Watch the event, but act on pace: compare the listing's and the market's forward pace for the dates.
2. When comparable forward pace is missing, keep the event on watch; do not move rates.
3. Weather alerts allow only hold, decrease, or flexibility (minimum stay, cancellation), never an increase.

chunks.heading: Do not

docs.title: Explaining markups and discounts to a client

chunks.text:
# Explaining markups and discounts to a client

- Kind: skill
- Area: communication
- Status: team decision — Fede's message to Spencer, 2026-10-09
- Owner: Fede (wording). The account owner sends it.
- Channels: Airbnb (markup and discounts), Vrbo (markup).
- Tools: Airbnb listing discounts page, PMS listing markups (e.g. Hospitable), PriceLabs target rate.
- When to use: after onboarding sets markups and discounts, or when a client asks why Airbnb shows discounts, whether discounts stack, or why the Airbnb price is higher than PriceLabs.
- Summary: Explain in one short message that PriceLabs sets the target, the channel markup (Airbnb 44% or 55%) absorbs fees and discounts, only one of length-of-stay, early bird or last minute applies, and the top-rated-guest discount is the one that stacks; show one worked example.

chunks.heading: Steps
chunks.text:
1. Check the live settings first: each listing's Airbnb and Vrbo markup in the PMS, and the discounts on Airbnb's discounts page. Never send numbers you have not seen on the listing.
2. Fill the template below. Say which markup each listing uses and why: 44% without the top-rated-guest discount, 55% with it. For listings coming out of slow bookings, say we turned the discount on for an extra exposure bump ([[skills/channel-discounts]]).
3. Keep the stacking explanation to two sentences ([[skills/channel-discounts]], "How Airbnb stacks them").
4. Use one worked example: a $100 target, or the listing's own target if the client prefers real numbers.
5. Add the taxes line only if pass-through taxes were set up ([[skills/taxes-pass-through]]).

chunks.heading: Message template
chunks.text:
**Your target rate and the markup**

PriceLabs sets your target nightly rate. Each channel adds a markup on top, so platform fees and discounts come out of the markup, not your target. Vrbo is [12]%.

On Airbnb we use one of two markups: **44%** when we don't use the top-rated-guest discount, **55%** when we do. [Reason, e.g.: Since your listings are coming out of a slow booking period, we turned on the top-rated-guest discount for an extra exposure bump in Airbnb search, so your listings are at 55%.]

**Your Airbnb discounts**

- Trip length: [21]% for 3+ nights, [22]% for 5+, [26]% for 14+
- Weekly (7+ nights): [24]%
- Monthly (28+ nights): [28]%
- Early bird (booked 1+ month ahead): [20]%
- Last minute (booked within 28 days): [20]%
- Top-rated guests (rated 4.8+ with 3+ reviews): [15]%

**How they combine**

Only one of the length-of-stay, early-bird or last-minute discounts applies to a booking. Airbnb picks length of stay first, so early bird and last minute only matter on 1–2 night stays. The top-rated-guest discount is the only one that adds on top.

**Example:** with a $100 PriceLabs target, Airbnb shows $155. A 7-night stay gets the weekly discount: $117.80 a night. A top-rated guest gets 15% more off: $100.13, right at your target. These are nightly prices before Airbnb's fees and taxes.

[If set up: **Taxes are separate:** the county taxes we set up show at checkout and come to you as their own "pass-through" payout line.]

chunks.heading: Example math (55% markup, $100 target, defaults)
chunks.text:
- 2 nights, booked 2 months out: early bird 20%, $124.00 (top-rated guest $105.40).
- 3 nights: trip length 21% outranks early bird, $122.45 (top-rated $104.08).
- 7 nights: weekly 24%, $117.80 (top-rated $100.13).
- 30 nights: monthly 28%, $111.60 (top-rated $94.86, a bit under target on purpose).
- With 44% (no top-rated discount): 7 nights is $144 × 0.76 = $109.44.

chunks.heading: Do not
chunks.text:
- Do not promise that a discount brings bookings or a ranking position: say "exposure bump", not a result.
- Do not quote a payout after Airbnb's fees: our numbers are guest-facing nightly prices before fees and taxes.
- Do not send a client another client's numbers.

chunks.heading: Decided / open
chunks.text:
- Decided: two Airbnb markups, 44% and 55% (Fede, 2026-10-09). Spencer's listings: both at 55%, Vrbo 12%.
- Open: Fede's review of the Hub article `airbnb-discounts-and-markups`.

# International taxes (Mexico first)

- Kind: framework
- Area: taxes
- Status: draft — from Fede's questions to Michelle Lohr on Hub ticket #84 (2026-10-09); Mexico details pending Fede
- Owner: Fede. The owner's accountant confirms what is owed.
- Channels: Airbnb first; check Vrbo and Booking.com per country.
- Tools: the owner's payout breakdown (screenshot), the channel's tax settings for that country.
- When to use: any listing outside the US, or an owner who is a tax resident of another country.
- Summary: Abroad, the platform may withhold income tax and VAT from the host's payout as well as charge taxes to the guest; separate the two, work out the owner's net per night, and use it for the price floor.

chunks.heading: Why it differs from the US
chunks.text:
- In the US, local taxes are mostly charged to the guest; the fix is collecting the missing ones as pass-through ([[skills/taxes-pass-through]]).
- Abroad, the platform may also take taxes from the host's payout. For a host resident in Mexico, Fede's understanding (to confirm with the owner): Airbnb withholds income tax and VAT from the payout. Those lower what the owner nets per night, which is why Michelle asked for a slow-season price floor (ticket #84).
- Tax residency changes the treatment: Michelle is a resident of Mexico (ticket #84, 2026-10-09).

chunks.heading: Steps
chunks.text:
1. Ask the owner for their tax residency, every tax they pay locally, and a payout breakdown. Fede's opening question: "Are there other taxes you are paying locally besides VAT on accommodation and the lodging tax?"
2. Separate taxes charged to the guest (collected at checkout) from taxes withheld from the host (taken from the payout).
3. Check which guest taxes the channel collects and remits, and add any missing one as pass-through ([[skills/taxes-pass-through]]).
4. Work out the owner's net per night after withholdings and channel fees, and feed it into [[skills/minimum-price-floor]].
5. Record each country's confirmed rules in a section below, with the date and source.

chunks.heading: Mexico (as of 2026-10-09, to confirm)
chunks.text:
- Guest-side: VAT on accommodation; Impuesto Sobre Hospedaje (state lodging tax), 6% per Fede's message.
- Host-side: Airbnb withholds income tax and VAT from a Mexico-resident host's payout (Fede's question; the owner's confirmation pending).
- Withholding rates: not on file.

chunks.heading: Do not
chunks.text:
- Do not assume the US pass-through setup covers taxes withheld from the payout.
- Do not give tax or legal advice: revenue advice only; the owner's accountant confirms.

chunks.heading: Decided / open
chunks.text: - Open: Fede to confirm Mexico's rates and rules; add other countries as they come up.

chunks.text: - Hub ticket #84 (Michelle Lohr, Playa del Carmen listings): her ask (2026-10-02, a slow-season price floor because of Mexican taxes) and Fede's tax questions (2026-10-09).

# Minimum price floor

- Kind: framework
- Area: rates
- Status: draft — Fede: a floor has to be reviewed over time (2026-10-09); how it is computed is pending Fede
- Owner: Fede. Andrés sets it in PriceLabs.
- Channels: all (the floor is set in PriceLabs before channel markups).
- Tools: PriceLabs minimum price and safety minimum price, the owner's payout breakdown.
- When to use: onboarding, each new season, or when an owner says a booking below some price is not worth taking.
- Summary: Set a per-listing, per-season floor from what the owner nets per night after channel fees and taxes, protect it in PriceLabs, and review it every season instead of setting it once.

chunks.heading: Steps
chunks.text:
1. Work out what the owner nets per night at a given rate: channel fees and markup ([[skills/ota-markup]]), taxes withheld from the payout ([[skills/international-taxes]]), and any tax still paid out of profit ([[skills/taxes-pass-through]]).
2. Agree the floor with the owner for each season. Examples on file: Spencer's winter minimums noted as $600/$550 (Mount Washington) and $900 (Horse Farm), reasons not on file; Michelle asked for a slow-season floor because of Mexican taxes (ticket #84).
3. Set it as the PriceLabs minimum price; use PriceLabs' safety minimum price to protect it (suggested on the Corzly call, 2026-08-04).
4. Review it every season and whenever taxes, fees, costs, or the market change.

chunks.heading: Do not
chunks.text:
- Do not set a floor once and forget it.
- Do not let a floor override slow-week discounts the owner has approved: check the two together (Michelle okayed lower October and early-November rates on her Mexico listings, ticket #137).

chunks.heading: Decided / open
chunks.text: - Open (Fede to set): how the floor is computed (cost-based, net payout target, or market-based), which costs go in, and the review schedule.

docs.title: Visibility recovery after a mid-term stay

chunks.text:
# Visibility recovery after a mid-term stay

- Kind: skill
- Area: visibility
- Status: draft — method from Fede's answer on Hub ticket #12, gaps answered 2026-10-09
- Owner: Fede (method). Andrés applies the rates; Martín uses the client wording.
- Channels: mostly Airbnb (its ranking leans on conversion). Vrbo and Booking.com: case by case.
- Tools: PriceLabs (rates), RankBreeze (visibility and conversion), the guest's MTR booking.
- When to use: a client asks why a listing gets few views, ranks low, or is "not visible", and the listing has a mid-term stay (MTR, about 30+ nights) coming up, running, or just ended. Also when planning rates around a confirmed MTR.
- Summary: After a mid-term stay, relaunch the listing like a new launch (competitive rates for 30 days of open calendar) to rebuild Airbnb conversion and ranking, without undercutting a possible extension.

chunks.heading: Why it happens
chunks.text:
- During an MTR, Airbnb records no new short-stay bookings for the listing for weeks.
- Conversion (search views that turn into bookings) is one of Airbnb's strongest ranking signals. With no recent conversions, the listing comes back ranked lower.

chunks.heading: Steps
chunks.text:
1. **Before the MTR:** keep competitive rates on the open dates before check-in, so the listing keeps converting until the stay starts.
2. **While an extension is possible:** hold the rates for dates after check-out where they are. A guest who is thinking about extending must not see lower rates on Airbnb.
3. **Extension check:** propose asking the MTR guest about an extension about 4 weeks before check-out (ticket #12: early April for a May check-out). That is the first proposal; adjust the timing to the client's response.
4. **After check-out, no extension:** treat the return like a new listing launch ([[skills/new-listing-launch]]). Use competitive rates for the first 30 days of open calendar after the stay, to win bookings fast, rebuild conversion, and regain ranking.
   - "Competitive" has no fixed number: set it from a separate analysis of where the market is at the time (comps, market occupancy and rates for those dates).
5. **After the 30 days:** step rates back up based on pickup and pacing, plus visibility and conversion against the market (check in [[stack/rankbreeze]]).
6. **Tell the client** in this shape: a bold "<property> visibility" title; the cause in two sentences (algorithm, conversion); the key idea (relaunch like a new listing); the plan split "Before the MTR stay" / "After the MTR stay"; the dated next step (the extension check).

chunks.heading: Do not
chunks.text:
- Do not promise a ranking position or a date when visibility comes back.
- Do not lower rates on dates the MTR guest could extend into before the extension is ruled out.
- Do not use this when there is no MTR: low visibility can also come from blocks, minimum stays, reviews, or listing quality. Check those first.

chunks.heading: Decided / open
chunks.text:
- Decided by Fede (2026-10-09): relaunch level has no fixed % or floor (a separate market analysis sets it each time); the extension check is first proposed about 4 weeks before check-out and adjusted to the client's response; rates step back up by pickup, pacing, and RankBreeze visibility and conversion; mostly Airbnb.
- Open: Fede's review of this page as a whole.

# New listing launch pricing

- Kind: framework
- Area: launch
- Status: team decision — 2026-06-11 launch markup; the rest stated in meetings (Evidence v2)
- Owner: Fede (rules). Andrés applies them.
- Channels: Airbnb (the new-listing discount is Airbnb's); the competitive-first-weeks rule applies to every channel.
- Tools: PriceLabs.
- When to use: a listing goes live for the first time, or comes back after a long gap (see [[skills/mtr-visibility-recovery]]).
- Summary: Launch only when the listing is fully ready, price competitively for the first 30–60 days to win bookings and reviews, and offset Airbnb's new-listing discount with a 20% markup that steps down.

chunks.heading: Steps
chunks.text:
1. Go live only when the listing is 100% ready, with professional photos.
2. Price competitively for the first 30–60 calendar days to win bookings and reviews. Far-out dates can carry a premium.
3. Airbnb gives new listings a 20% discount for the first guests. Mark base rates up 20% from day 1, drop the markup to 10% after 30 days out, and remove it after the first 3 bookings.
4. Price new or renovated properties to market potential and last year's market pacing, not to the owner's prior-year numbers ([[skills/no-history-pricing]]).

chunks.heading: Do not
chunks.text:
- Do not launch an unfinished listing to "test the market".
- Do not lock in low rates on far-out peak dates during the launch window (one client opened 45 days out at a 20% discount to avoid locking low holiday rates).

chunks.heading: Decided / open
chunks.text:
- Decided: the launch markup applies from day 1 on every new listing ([[decisions/2026-06-11-new-listing-launch-markup]]).
- Open: how "competitive" is set in numbers (see the market-analysis note in [[skills/mtr-visibility-recovery]]).

- Kind: framework

chunks.text:

2. Use last year's **market** pacing, not the owner's pacing.
3. Set a 12-month revenue target split by month for each property.
4. Run quarterly pacing reviews and flag properties 15–20% behind target.

# OTA markup and Airbnb discounts

- Kind: framework
- Area: channels
- Status: approved — Hub knowledge article, client-safe
- Owner: Fede.
- Channels: Airbnb (markup set through the PMS, e.g. Hospitable).
- Tools: PriceLabs, PMS channel markup, Airbnb reservation breakdown.

chunks.heading: Steps
chunks.text:
1. Send the target rate from PriceLabs through the PMS.
2. Apply an Airbnb channel markup before Airbnb applies the eligible promotion (example: $100 target + 44% markup = $144; a 20% discount gives $115.20 before fees and taxes).
3. Two Airbnb markups: **44%** without the top-rated-guest discount, **55%** with it (Fede, 2026-10-09; [[skills/channel-discounts]]). Vrbo: 12% on Spencer's listings (other listings: check the PMS).
4. Before quoting exact numbers, verify the live markup, discount, accommodation subtotal, guest total, and host payout.
